📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 24 Nov 2026 06:58.

Mauricio Pochettino has been handed a 'limited' winter transfer budget as he looks to turn Manchester United's season around with reinforcements.

The newly introduced Red Devils boss is expected to have the funds for just two January signings, despite several areas of his squad requiring attention.

United's financial restrictions could therefore leave the Argentine facing some difficult decisions when the transfer window opens.

According to the Daily Mail, Pochettino will have less than £50m to spend in January, with United's financial position and the Premier League's new financial rules restricting their spending power.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss admitted that United are in a relegation battle after beginning his tenure with a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield, leaving the club second from bottom.

The expectation is that Pochettino will be able to make two additions, potentially including a loan signing, although sources have not completely ruled out United gambling on further investment if their relegation threat becomes more serious.

It has been revealed that central defence is an obvious priority following the Anfield defeat, with Brentford's Nathan Collins emerging as a strong candidate. Calvin Bassey is another option, although he is expected to sign a latest Fulham contract, while Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite is valued at more than £70m.

United are also interested in strengthening at left-back, having previously been linked with Barcelona's Alejandro Balde and Manchester City's Rayan Ait-Nouri.

A striker is another consideration, particularly with Benjamin Sesko sidelined by a shin injury. However, Ivan Toney's reported £500,000-a-week wages make him an unrealistic option, while Leeds United are keen to extend Dominic Calvert-Lewin's £180,000-a-week contract.

A budget below £50m, alongside the expectation of only two additions, makes it difficult to see United addressing all three areas in January.

A move for someone like Lewis Hall at left-back or Branthwaite at centre-back would seemingly be beyond their financial reach, particularly if Newcastle and Everton demand substantial fees.

However, Balde and RB Leipzig's David Raum could represent more budget-friendly alternatives, depending on their respective clubs' willingness to negotiate.

The bigger question is whether United can afford to strengthen centrally and up front as well. Collins could be a realistic defensive target, but finding the funds for another centre-back and a striker on top of that looks particularly difficult at this stage.

Unless United generate significant funds through player sales, Pochettino may have to prioritise two positions and make the best of the squad he inherits.

That is a worrying prospect for a behemoth of a club currently fighting to avoid relegation.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has warned Ethan Nwaneri that brief flashes of quality will not be enough to secure regular football at Borussia Dortmund.
  • The record-breaking 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga leaders on loan from the Gunners in the summer, but has struggled for opportunities in recent weeks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 24 Nov 2026 07:16.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has warned Ethan Nwaneri that brief flashes of quality will not be enough to secure regular football at Borussia Dortmund.

The record-breaking 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga leaders on loan from the Gunners in the summer, but has struggled for opportunities in recent weeks.

Nwaneri could now face his parent club in Tuesday's Champions League meeting in north London, with Arteta making his expectations clear.

Nwaneri initially enjoyed opportunities in Niko Kovac's starting lineup after arriving in Germany, but his involvement has since diminished significantly.

The versatile attacking midfielder has not started a match in over a month and has played just five minutes across Dortmund's last three Bundesliga fixtures.

Arteta believes the teenager must show greater consistency to establish himself at the highest level, insisting that occasional impressive performances are not enough.

Industry observers note that "We're talking here about the highest level in Europe," the Arsenal boss mentioned (via the Evening Standard). "You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency.".

The Spaniard also stressed that Nwaneri must earn his place in a talented Dortmund squad, rather than expect opportunities because of his Arsenal background.

"He needs to earn the right to play," Arteta added, explaining that joining a major European club does not automatically guarantee minutes.

Arteta remains convinced that Nwaneri has the mentality and quality to succeed, but acknowledged that his loan spells at Marseille and Dortmund form part of a challenging development journey.

Arsenal are understood to have the option to recall the youngster in January if his situation does not improve, with Arteta right now unconvinced that the Dortmund move is delivering the desired benefits.

Nwaneri is eligible to feature against his parent club on Tuesday, although Dortmund's strong form makes a starting place appear unlikely.

Nevertheless, the opportunity to face Arsenal off the bench could provide the teenager with an ideal platform to respond to Arteta's comments, particularly after his recent lack of involvement.

Industry observers note that the Gunners boss has challenged him to show consistency and earn his place, rather than rely on occasional moments of quality. A positive contribution against the Premier League champions would certainly help his case.

Should Nwaneri find the net, he could join a select group of players to score against their parent clubs while on loan, including James Rodriguez against Real Madrid and Philippe Coutinho against Barcelona during their respective spells at Bayern Munich.

It would be a significant way to make his mark, although simply earning meaningful minutes against Arsenal would represent an encouraging step in his Dortmund journey.

Breaking: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1294 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that young people pose inside a crematorium oven at the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial, laughing while they give the Nazi salute and take pictures of each other.
  • "Incidents like this have become more frequent in recent years.
  • Wagner is part of the curatorial team behind the exhibition "Never Again!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that young people pose inside a crematorium oven at the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial, laughing while they give the Nazi salute and take pictures of each other. "In a sense, they're trophies to post on social media for them to boast about — breaking the ultimate taboo," Jens-Christian Wagner, director of the Buchenwald and Mittelbau-Dora Memorials Foundation, told DW.

"Incidents like this have become more frequent in recent years. We have seen memorial trees planted in honor of concentration camp victims cut down. When something like this happens — and it happens regularly — I find it particularly despicable because, because it ultimately kills these people a second time," added Wagner.

Wagner is part of the curatorial team behind the exhibition "Never Again! Against Forgetting the Crimes of the Nazi Regime" in Bonn's Bundeskunsthalle, or the Art and Exhibition Hall of the Federal Republic of Germany. Wagner stated Holocaust remembrance is under pressure, and the subject of intensifying attacks.

Critics have dismissed remembrance as a "cult of guilt" or "national masochism." With right-wing populism on the rise and historical revisionism becoming more common, Wagner worries about how Germany will remember the victims murdered by the Nazi regime. He is also concerned about the future of democracy. And soon, there will be no Holocaust survivors left to tell the true story of what happened.

This upcoming exhibition tackles this concern head-on with numerous works of art and historical artifacts.

Recent findings suggest that "I hope that perhaps even some people who don't already believe it's important to confront Nazi crimes will find their way to the exhibition," Wagner stated. Memorial sites also attract visitors who aren't necessarily convinced of the need to confront these parts of history. Many of them are students.

"Let's not kid ourselves: When a teacher says 'We're going there,' it's always a mandatory visit," he mentioned.

Industry observers note that for today's young people, the Nazi era seems like the distant past, Wagner explained. "When you tell them to remember something that their grandparents didn't even experience, it naturally feels like an emotional burden. They can practically see the finger being wagged at them, and that doesn't exactly encourage learning.".

A two-hour lecture won't have much of an impact if pupils aren't even paying attention. Instead, Buchenwald organizes full-day programs that allow students to explore historical sources together and make sense of history for themselves.

The next step, Wagner said, is to show young people that this chapter of history isn't closed. Visitors are encouraged to make connections between the past and current events like migration, for example.

Recent findings suggest that "For the longest time, people have been discussing migration almost exclusively in terms of threats to public safety and crime. This broadly marginalizes certain groups — a mechanism that also worked for National Socialism," he mentioned.

Eva Umlauf, 83, knows firsthand what it means to experience exclusion in its most extreme form. She is a patron of the Bonn exhibition.

In November 1944, Umlauf was just 2 years old when she, her pregnant mother and her father were deported by the Nazis from the Novaky labor camp in Slovakia to Auschwitz-Birkenau, the notorious Nazi concentration and extermination camp. She was saved from the gas chambers by mere days; the Nazis stopped using the chambers as the Red Army advanced, hoping to hide evidence of their crimes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that the camp was liberated on January 27, 1945. Three months later, Umlauf's sister Nora was born. But her father, her mother's siblings and her grandparents were all murdered. Eva barely survived herself. She suffered from tuberculosis, rickets and whooping cough, as well as edema caused by starvation. "Forget about the child. She won't survive," a doctor told her mother. But he was wrong.

It has been revealed that her mother returned to what was then Czechoslovakia with her two daughters, settling in Trencin. Eva Umlauf has no conscious memories of Auschwitz, but she carries her family's trauma deep within her.

Her mother never talked about what happened. Even so, Eva knew from an early age that she was a survivor. Her family rarely mentioned the camp by name, but one sentence came up again and again: "They stayed there." Eva knew that meant "they" were dead. And then, there was the number tattooed onto her arm: A26959.

Recent findings suggest that her mother taught her daughters not to draw attention to their Jewish identity — antisemitism was widespread throughout Czechoslovakia at the time. The small family managed to avoid harassment.

Eva Umlauf wanted to become a pediatrician, so she studied medicine. In the 1960s, she met her future husband, Jakob, who had also survived the Holocaust. He was an architect, active in Munich's Jewish community. They married in 1966, and she moved to Germany. She could hardly have imagined that she would one day live in the country of the perpetrators. "I don't hate Germans," she remarked. "But I cannot forgive. How can you forgive the deaths of 6 million people?".

In a recent development, it wasn't until much later that she first spoke publicly about the horrors of her early childhood. In 2011, she delivered a commemorative speech in Auschwitz on the anniversary of the camp's liberation. Since 2025, she has served as chair of the International Auschwitz Committee. A heart attack in 2014 motivated her to write her first book. "I was in intensive care. I thought to myself: If I get out of here healthy, I'll write a book.".

It has been revealed that her memoir, "The Number on Your Forearm is Blue Like Your Eyes," was first released in 2016. The English translation followed in 2024. Since its publication, hardly a day has passed without someone asking Eva Umlauf to share her story.

Sources indicate that she is appalled by the disrespectful behavior of young people at former concentration camps and by growing ignorance about the Holocaust. Sometimes, people even ask if she's too old to have a tattoo. But she also recalls a young man on the Munich subway who noticed the number on her arm and told her: "I want to apologize to you for what my ancestors did to you.".

Sources indicate that umlauf never imagined that antisemitism would once again become so widespread in Europe and the United States. Nor did she expect the rise of Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party.

"I go into schools. I'm so overwhelmed by the number of requests asking for my availability. And yet, the AfD is growing faster than I can reach students. It makes me think all this work is for nothing," she told DW.

Sources indicate that germany must never again fall under a right-wing dictatorship, she stressed. "'Never again' sounds nice, but all I can say is: It's happening again! Wouldn't 'Here We Go Again: Never Again' make a good title for the exhibition?".

It has been revealed that she also shared her message to young people in the exhibition catalog, "Never Again": "You are not responsible for the crimes of your grandparents and great-grandparents. But you are responsible for the future. […] You are the generation that will shape our world. Make it a place where everyone can grow up safely, regardless of their background, faith or skin color.".

In a recent development, she continues: "You don't have to be perfect. You just have to stay alert. Take care of your country.".

In a recent development, the exhibition "Never Again! Against Forgetting the Crimes of the Nazi Regime" in the Bundeskunsthalle in Bonn runs through May 2, 2027.

This article was originally written in German.

#174749. AI is ditching hallucinated references — and other bad habits

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (812 w)

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

AI is ditching hallucinated references — and other bad habits

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (812 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hallucinated academic citations have become a hallmark of the artificial-intelligence era.
  • The finding is part of an analysis that reports that many LLM tendencies, such as overthinking simple mathematics problems and complying with illogical requests, fade over time as AI companies release upcoming or updated models with improved capabilities.
  • “We, as customers of these systems, need to not have such a fixed view of what AI can do and what it can’t do,” indicates co-author Owen Queen, an AI researcher at Stanford University in California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Credit: FabrikaSimf/Shutterstock.

Hallucinated academic citations have become a hallmark of the artificial-intelligence era. But they might soon be gone for good. Researchers have found that the latest large language models (LLMs) rarely, if ever, attribute information to sources that don’t exist.

The finding is part of an analysis that reports that many LLM tendencies, such as overthinking simple mathematics problems and complying with illogical requests, fade over time as AI companies release upcoming or updated models with improved capabilities. Many of these tendencies disappear about 16 months after the phenomenon is first described in a published paper. The analysis, described in a blogpost, has not been peer reviewed.

“We, as customers of these systems, need to not have such a fixed view of what AI can do and what it can’t do,” indicates co-author Owen Queen, an AI researcher at Stanford University in California.

Sources indicate that but just because an LLM behaviour fades as models improve doesn’t mean that the effect immediately disappears, notes Maxim Topaz, a health-care AI researcher at Columbia University in New York City. Topaz has found1 that the number of hallucinated citations in academic papers has risen drastically since 2023, probably because more researchers than ever before are using LLMs, and they often aren’t using the latest models.

Industry observers note that queen and his colleague identified 50 widely cited LLM behaviours that were described in publications between late 2022, when some of the first LLMs became widely available, and late 2025. They then gave the same prompts that first elicited the behaviour in the original publications to 20 LLMs that were released from mid-2024 to late 2026 to see if the effect has strengthened or weakened over time. For example, they asked each model to count the number of r’s in ‘strawberry’ — something that LLMs have found difficult but can now do more reliably.

According to recent reports, nearly half of the behaviours they checked have largely disappeared from newer models, leading the researchers to deem those effects ‘expired’. Expired behaviours had an average lifespan of about 16 months after publication, although some were fleeting — models stopped overthinking simple maths problems just a month and a half after this tendency was published. Other traits persisted, such as the stereotyping of Black women by disproportionately describing them as resilient, which lasted for longer than three years.

According to recent reports, although most of the retested LLM behaviours have faded over time, three have become more pronounced. Today’s models praise what their users like even more often than they used to, LLMs favour their own writing more strongly than that of other LLMs and people; and LLMs are now even worse than they used to be at generating truly random numbers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 07:45.

Noni Madueke's signing by Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had even stepped onto the pitch.

Arriving from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing and had to justify an investment in a player who initially seemed destined to be a back-up.

Sources indicate that A little over a year later, the debate is taking on another dimension. With Saka injured, Madueke has been given a longer run of opportunities and has taken the chance. As well as goals and assists, he has contributed in different roles on both sides of the pitch. The 2-2 draw with Newcastle, in which he scored the goal that earned Arsenal a point, was another example of this development.

Mikel Arteta has noticed a change that goes beyond productivity. In a press conference, the manager highlighted the variety that the forward has added to the team's play and his contribution without the ball. And Madueke's growth has followed a concrete path.

Industry observers note that madueke has very specific characteristics. Left-footed and explosive, he likes to receive the ball wide on the right, run at the full-back and carry the ball towards the box to shoot or find a team-mate. His short burst of acceleration and ability to change direction make his movements hard to defend when he receives the ball in equal-numbers situations.

That characteristic was already visible at Chelsea. In the 2024-25 season, he was one of the Premier League players who carried the ball into the box the most and created danger mainly through individual runs. The problem was inconsistency in execution: he did not always choose the best moment. Arteta acknowledged the change.

Sources indicate that 'He is becoming decisive in games, and that is what we need from our forward players. And he is doing it in several ways, which is something I really like. He has added variety and a lot more connection to his game' - Arteta said.

Industry observers note that the numbers help to gauge the growth. According to FotMob's analysis for the 2026-27 Premier League, Madueke creates 3.6 chances per 90 minutes, compared with 1.5 for Saka. It is a significant difference, although it is vital to consider that Saka has played fewer minutes.

The improvement also demonstrates in his ability to contribute without the ball. According to Arteta, Madueke does not always need to receive the ball at his feet to take part in the move.

It has been revealed that 'And yes, I also love his intensity without the ball. So, I would say he is becoming a much more complete player, and I think he is enjoying it a lot' - Arteta noted.

It has been revealed that the evolution, therefore, is not about abandoning the dribble but about knowing when to use it. Madueke remains a player of individual initiative, only now he seems to understand better how his actions can connect with the collective workings of the team.

The comparison with Saka is inevitable, but the two are not identical players. Both are left-footed and prefer to start from the right to cut inside, but they do so in different ways.

Saka is more refined in decision-making. He has excellent ball control, protects possession under pressure and alternates between carries, short passes and crosses very naturally. His ability to draw two markers and find the free team-mate is also one of Arsenal's main attacking tools.

Madueke, for his part, offers more explosiveness in the first movement and tends to look for the individual duel more often. He is a more vertical player, who likes to accelerate and attack the space left by the full-back. When he is confident, he can disorganise a defence without depending on a long build-up.

The creation data helps illustrate this difference. As well as outperforming Saka in chances created per 90 minutes in FotMob's analysis, Madueke also shows a greater volume of dribbles and progressive carries per minute in another statistical comparison this season. Saka, on the other hand, keeps the advantage in shooting and defensive contribution indicators. They are complementary profiles, not necessarily competitors for a single way of playing.

This difference is valuable for Arteta. Against opponents who defend in a low block, Saka can be more useful to control possession, combine with the midfielders and find the pass that dismantles the marking. Madueke can offer a more direct threat, attacking the full-back and creating situations of individual imbalance.

The Englishman has also shown that he can play on the left, a role he performed when Christos Tzolis was unavailable. There, he needs to adapt his movements: instead of cutting inside with his dominant foot, he can look for the byline and cross with his right. It is not necessarily his ideal position, but the versatility widens Arteta's options and prevents the team from depending on a single alternative for each side.

The competition with Saka, therefore, does not need to be understood as an attempt to take the starter's place. Arsenal need more than one player capable of deciding matches, especially in a long season, with the Premier League, the Champions League and domestic cups. The point is that Madueke is starting to offer arguments to be considered more than a simple replacement.

One detail of this transformation happened away from Arsenal. After being left out of an England squad, Madueke decided to use the international break to train individually. Instead of treating the period as a chance to rest, the forward sought out a specific preparation programme.

Arteta highlighted the player's reaction as an example for the rest of the squad. The manager stated that Madueke came back from the break as a different athlete, determined not to accept the situation he was in.

Madueke at Arsenal, season by season.

Premier League 2025-26 vs. 2026-27, per-90 averages.

Sources indicate that premier League games only. Because the seasons have different numbers of minutes, the comparison uses per-90 averages; the total appears below each average. The change compares the averages. Madueke has not yet provided an assist in the Premier League in 2026-27. Data up to 21 November 2026 (matchweek 11).

According to recent reports, 'He went away, decided to train, came back, and he was a different Noni. You could sense that he meant business, and he was not going to accept that situation. Since then, he has been incredible' - Arteta explained, commenting on the player's change of attitude.

The individual work, however, did not start now. In an interview with Sky Sports, Madueke revealed that he has been working for years with specialist coach Saul Isaksson-Hurst, since his time at PSV. The partnership involves technical improvement and individual development, with special attention to the ability to be more decisive in the final third.

Industry observers note that the result has shown up in the numbers: his average of chances created has more than doubled compared with last season, reaching 3.57 per 90 minutes in the Premier League. His dribble success rate has risen from 50% to 55%, while his passing accuracy has gone from 78% to 87%. In open-play crosses, his success rate has jumped from 14% to 33%.

These numbers help explain why Arteta talks about a more complete player. Madueke has not stopped looking for the dribble, but he has started to execute better other actions that previously could limit his influence. The progress has come from different reasons and paths, but the result has arrived and is evident in the current season.

Why Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy matters for AI race

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1123 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's admission to an affair with a woman whom US intelligence officials believe was working as a spy for China could have profound implications for the $5 trillion (€4.47 trillion) company.
  • The Financial Times first reported on Huang's affair with Alice H., an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia, which has been suspected of trying to circumvent export controls to get advanced Nvidia chips into China.
  • The newspaper reported that the US government and its intelligence community believe she was recruited as a spy by China's Ministry of State Security intelligence agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's admission to an affair with a woman whom US intelligence officials believe was working as a spy for China could have profound implications for the $5 trillion (€4.47 trillion) company.

The Financial Times first reported on Huang's affair with Alice H., an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia, which has been suspected of trying to circumvent export controls to get advanced Nvidia chips into China.

The newspaper reported that the US government and its intelligence community believe she was recruited as a spy by China's Ministry of State Security intelligence agency.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US government officials drafted a memo about the allegations shortly before US President Donald Trump traveled to Beijing for a summit with Xi Jinping in May.

Huang's relationship with the alleged Chinese spy has exposed him and the tech giant to criticism that it may have allowed China to obtain valuable trade secrets as Beijing tries to gain an edge in the race to develop advanced AI models.

It has been revealed that nvidia is initiating an investigation led by independent board members and an external law firm. It said in a statement that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.".

It has been revealed that "The board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders," the tech giant said Sunday. "While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board's inquiry will examine all available information.".

The manufacturer's shares fell in early trading on Monday.

While US intelligence officials have not commented publicly on the claims, Trump — with whom Jensen Huang has a close relationship — has backed the Nvidia boss.

"He's an honorable guy," mentioned Trump. "I have not spoken to him ​about it. I just know he's a ​fine person, but you never know what is going on. I hope everything's fine.".

Tim Culpan, an Asia tech reporter who has covered Nvidia and Huang closely for years, told DW that while Nvidia's fundamental strengths as a company remain in place, Huang is hugely personally damaged by the story.

"They're still going to make great chips and they're going to sell them to millions of customers around the world who want the best AI chips in the world," he remarked.

"His opinion is going to carry a lot less weight now. And that, in the long term, will flow through to Nvidia and Nvidia's own corporate interests. So it won't be immediate. It's really a fact that he doesn't have the sway or the power that he might have had one week ago simply through this.".

Richard Windsor, a tech analyst and the founder of research tech giant Radio Free Mobile, said the news could be very serious for Nvidia given how much the company has revolved around Huang for decades.

"This problem is particularly acute because Jensen Huang is very hands-on, meaning that the key decisions that led to its success were ultimately taken by him and because there is no obvious successor," he mentioned.

"I suspect we are about to find out just how much the market thinks that the company is dependent on its iconic founder and CEO.".

Nvidia and Huang's attitude toward China and potential Chinese customers has been a bone of contention with US intelligence officials — despite Huang's close relationship with Trump.

Industry observers note that huang has repeatedly lobbied Trump to ease restrictions on the sale of Nvidia chips to China. A 2025 export control deal heavily curbed sales, but Trump subsequently permitted the export of older H200 Nvidia chips to China in return for the US government receiving a cut of the sales.

However, that deal has been complicated and bogged down by Washington's strict export-license review. China has also initiated import controls, despite strong demand from Chinese companies. China lacks access to the most advanced AI-capable chips. Beijing wants to develop its own alternatives but has struggled to catch up.

Huang has argued that Chinese dependence on Nvidia's chips would prevent rivals such as Huawei from catching up and boosting China's ambitions to dominate AI supply chains.

However, that argument has been dismissed by many US intelligence officials. They fear that unlimited Chinese access to the most advanced Nvidia chips would boost China's domestic AI sector, lead to its AI models catching up with the leading US models and see the chips being used in Chinese military applications.

The US-China rivalry has become a central theme in the global AI story, with both countries seeking to gain an upper hand in the technology. Leading US AI executives such as Anthropic's Dario Amodei have argued that US AI companies can't afford to take a prolonged pause to allow safety standards in AI to catch up, if they're going to prevent Chinese firms from gaining an advantage.

Washington's central fear over Huang's affair is that it could have led to Beijing obtaining vital trade secrets or other key information about how Nvidia makes its most advanced chips.

Recent findings suggest that windsor thinks Huang will survive the "severe test" due to his importance to the manufacturer. He also cast doubt on the extent to which Beijing and its leading tech firms have learned from Nvidia's chips, pointing to China's own chip ambitions and commitment to have its firms buy its own semiconductors.

"I am far from convinced that Chinese AI has materially benefited from technology or illicit chip imports that it gained from Nvidia," he remarked.

The news comes at a particularly challenging moment for Nvidia, which has benefited massively from the AI boom thanks to its position as the leading maker of cutting-edge semiconductors needed for AI applications.

Nvidia's valuation has soared dramatically in recent years as companies rushed to buy its chips, becoming the world's first $5 trillion tech giant in October 2025.

According to recent reports, however, doubts over the sustainability of the $9 trillion capital expenditure AI boom have sparked a major sell-off in stocks related to the boom in recent weeks. The Democrats' sweeping victories in the US midterms have added to the doubts, given the strength of voter opposition to data center construction in the US.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 08:40, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 08:42.

James Tarkowski received his first-ever red card in the Premier League as Everton fell to a heavy 4-0 defeat at Brentford on Monday night.

The 34-year-old defender had previously been given 74 yellow cards across 350 Premier League appearances but had never been sent off – a top-flight record for the most yellows without ever seeing red.

However, Tarkowski was dismissed in the first half with the Toffees trailing by two goals at the Gtech Community Stadium for a studs-up challenge on the shin of Yehor Yarmolyuk.

Tarkowski had initially thundered into a sliding challenge and won the ball, but his right boot followed through with his studs scraping down the Brentford midfielder’s leg.

On-field referee Craig Pawson gave a yellow card for the challenge, but was then advised by VAR to review the incident at the pitchside monitor, where he ultimately came to the decision to upgrade the yellow to a red.

Tarkowski was deemed to have “committed a challenge that endangers his opponent's safety” with a red card issued for serious foul play.

Sources indicate that james Tarkowski is sent off! ? https://t.co/s5ta4f74np.

Tarkowski will therefore serve a three-match suspension and will crucially miss Sunday’s Merseyside derby against rivals Liverpool at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The Toffees captain is also banned for a trip to Aston Villa on December 2 and a home clash with Fulham four days later, but he is available to return for an away fixture against Brighton & Hove Albion on December 13.

After taking charge of his record-breaking 593rd game as Everton manager, David Moyes was asked whether the club will look to appeal the red card, and he told Sky Sports: "Don't know yet.

"I thought Tarki got the ball in plenty of time, certainly got there before the player who came in late, but I think Tarki's foot was high, and in that case then there is a chance it can be given.".

According to recent reports, speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Moyes added: "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was, but when I've looked at it again I think his foot high. Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that.".

Sky Sports pundit and former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher believes that Tarkowski was right to be sent off and feels that Moyes has a “massive problem” to deal with ahead of the Merseyside derby.

"It is a red card. It might not have been a red card in 1996, but it is in 2026,” Carragher said on Monday Night Football.

"He knows what he's doing, and he doesn't need to do that. At the last moment, he is trying to pull back on the intensity of the challenge. Don't give [the referee] the option. He doesn't need to do that. I've made tackles like that.".

He added: "David Moyes should be looking at him and thinking [it's 2-0], you've left your mates out there with 10, and it's the Merseyside derby next.

Recent findings suggest that "For me, it's the biggest game of the season. Everton, biggest game of the season. I hope for the Liverpool players and staff, the biggest game of the season.

"He's brilliant in the box, and that will be a big problem for Everton. He's so good set-piece-wise.".

Either Jake O'Brien or Michael Keane is expected to play at centre-back alongside Jarrad Branthwaite in the absence of Tarkowski in the next three Premier League games.

A four-goal defeat for Everton has seen them slip to ninth in the Premier League table, with Brentford leapfrogging them into seventh position, albeit sitting just one point above them.

Kerkez arrived with two Premier League seasons behind him, while Svensson would have to adapt to a new league and a new system. Liverpool should buy a right-back first and hold a ceiling of around £35m for Svensson, because above that they would repeat the Kerkez gamble with less evidence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 08:45.

Recent findings suggest that paris Saint-Germain could indirectly do Barcelona a favour in the January transfer window. In search of a potential attacking reinforcement after the long-term injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, the capital club have drawn up an initial shortlist.

Industry observers note that according to AS, Antonio Nusa is among the capital club's preferred targets, alongside Abde Ezzalzouli, Gianluca Prestianni, Ibrahim Maza, Luis Diaz and Estevao. These players will be difficult to sign in the January transfer window. Paris have already experienced that, having been rebuffed over Estevao, while Prestianni wants to finish the season at Benfica.

Sources indicate that in that sense, Abde Ezzalzouli could be an interesting option. 3Cat confirms that the Morocco international is among the targets being studied by PSG to strengthen their attack in January. Aged 24, Abde is enjoying a good start to the season, with four goals and one assist in 13 games for the Andalusian club.

His profile has reportedly caught the attention of the Parisian hierarchy, especially as the player now shares the same agent as Achraf Hakimi.

This could ease discussions. The rumour is also being followed closely in Barcelona, as a potential transfer of the Real Betis winger would allow Barcelona to recoup a significant sum.

The Catalan outlet recalls that in September 2023, Barcelona sold Abde to Real Betis for £6.4m (€7.5m). In that deal, they kept a share of the Moroccan's economic rights. Initially set at 50%, it was later reduced to 20% in February 2025 as part of the agreement concerning Vitor Roque.

According to recent reports, A £51m (€60m) transfer, the amount of Abde's release clause, would therefore bring Barcelona £10m. PSG would have the opportunity to sign a promising 24-year-old winger for a reasonable amount, while doing their Spanish rivals a serious financial favour by triggering the clause.

This sum could give the Barcelona hierarchy more room for manoeuvre to strengthen Hansi Flick's squad this winter. The German boss is notably looking to sign a centre-back.

It should be noted that, at this stage, no agreement or advanced negotiation has been unveiled for Abde's arrival at PSG. It remains to be seen whether Paris will actually take action.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026.

When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the new head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

Industry observers note that however, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

At a meeting of the club’s executive committee on November 5 – after United had lost to Chelsea and staged a chaotic Champions League win against Roma – it was decided that Pochettino would be the No.1 choice if Carrick was sacked.

By the time the Argentine caught that flight to Atlanta 24 hours later to take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, United were preparing to make their move.

This is the story of the whirlwind two weeks that will end with Pochettino taking charge of his first game as United boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday following the dramatic events on both sides of the Atlantic.

Patrick Dorgu’s injury-time header rescued United from another defeat as they snatched a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, but it wasn’t enough to save Carrick. His fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp.

There is a five-hour time difference between Manchester and Georgia, so it was late afternoon when Pochettino first learned of United’s interest at the Trilith Guesthouse – close to the US national team’s training base in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta – as the players began to report there for duty.

Michael Carrick's fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

As speculation raged over Carrick’s future, the odds on Pochettino replacing him at Old Trafford were slashed after some significant money was placed on the 54-year-old overnight.

Industry observers note that preliminary talks continued with his representatives who made the US Soccer Federation aware of the situation. Pochettino discussed it over dinner at the team hotel with chief executive JT Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich who knew it was pointless trying to change his mind.

‘That was the significant day,’ says a source close to Pochettino, who took US team training in Fayetteville. ‘It became real and the optimism grew.’.

As talks accelerated between United and their prospective new head coach, Carrick returned to Carrington to work with the United players not on international duty while chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and rubber-stamp the change.

United reached verbal agreement with Pochettino over a two-and-a-half-year deal, and agreed to pay US Soccer around £10million to buy the 54-year-old and his staff – No 2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott – out of their contracts.

There was never any question of him leaving before the two Haiti ties, even though it left little time before his first game against Liverpool. Pochettino is noted to have been respectful of the USA’s position and felt an obligation to see the job through.

As a compromise, it was agreed that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr would be allowed to leave for Manchester after the first leg regardless of the result.

According to recent reports, media in the US were informed that access to the players had been cancelled out of respect for Veterans Day. It also meant that they don’t have to answer questions about Pochettino’s future.

Carrick returned to Carrington at 7.50am for the last time as United head coach and was sacked in a meeting with Berrada and Wilcox.

By the time Pochettino woke up in Fayetteville, United officially had a managerial vacancy and he gathered the players together for a scheduled team briefing at 10am.

Pochettino went through the usual pre-match preparation, and then invited staff into the room for the second half of the meeting.

Recent findings suggest that there was some emotion but no surprise when he informed them of his decision to take the United job. ‘As you’d expect, he spoke from the heart,’ says a source. ‘He loved being here but United was a dream opportunity. It was too hard to say no, but hard to say goodbye.’.

United officially announced Pochettino’s appointment and confirmed that he would stay in charge for the USA’s two games against Haiti before starting work the following Wednesday.

Pochettino conducted his pre-match press conference in Fayetteville, flanked by CEO chief JT Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, and broke down in tears as he thanked them for their support over the last 26 months.

Otherwise, the preparation is said to have gone according to strategy as the US squad flew to Miami.

The Argentine broke down in tears as he thanked the USA for their support over the last 26 months.

In a recent development, the US smashed Haiti 6-0 to all but guarantee their place in the semi-finals. Even so the message from Pochettino to his players after the game was: ‘This tie isn’t over.’.

The players learned for the first time that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr were leaving camp, and they headed straight to Manchester.

Pochettino flew with the players from Miami to Cincinnati for the second leg at the TQL Stadium.

On a visit to the Kenwood Towne Centre shopping mall, a man whose profile had risen in the US during his two years in charge of the national team was approached by even more fans than normal.

When Pochettino appeared as a guest of honour at the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium that night, a number of Bengals’ players and staff congratulated him on his new job claiming to be United fans.

It emerged that United had provided a private jet for Pochettino and the remainder of his staff to fly straight from Cincinnati to Manchester through the night after the second leg.

In his pre-match press conference, he confirmed the departure of his three coaches over the weekend, and it was no surprise to learn that he was in constant contact over several days as he prepared to join them at Carrington.

Recent findings suggest that the US beat Haiti by two goals to complete an 8-0 aggregate win. Afterwards, they played Take Me Home, Country Roads by John Denver over the stadium PA, which has been a tradition since the US hosted the World Cup last summer but carried particular poignance given that it has also been adopted as an anthem at United.

Pochettino invited all the staff onto the pitch for a team photo as he led a chant of U-S-A, and there was a tearful send-off in the dressing-room as he was presented with a signed shirt and a special hand-painted bottle of Clase Azul tequila.

It’s a favourite tipple of Pochettino’s and staff also ordered food from Chick-fil-A, which Pochettino regrets won’t be available in Manchester.

He never had a permanent residence in America, so he left the stadium at 10.30pm with the same suitcase he had brought from London and headed for Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport for the flight to Manchester.

Pochettino had a poor night’s sleep before landing shortly before noon aboard the grey Gulfstream G700 jet with D’Agostino, Scott and Tuya.

He posted a picture from the skies above Manchester and was then driven to Carrington, changing into an official United tracksuit en route.

Pochettino was too late for training but met with some of the players and club executives before being given a tour of the training ground and conducting an interview with MUTV which wrapped up about 7pm. He stayed at the training ground long into the evening to catch up on his preparation for Liverpool.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United.

It has been revealed that more players returned from international duty, but Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online. It was proof – if he needed it – that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will be under even greater scrutiny at United.

Responding, Pochettino said: 'We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.

In a recent development, 'What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?

'I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about.'.

Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online.

Having only trained for a couple of hours on Thursday, Pochettino worked with the players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

‘The training session was a little bit longer than it normally is in (match day) minus two,’ stated Pochettino at his opening pre-match press conference, admitting that he had not even had a chance to shower beforehand.

Pochettino worked with his new players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

Pochettino took training for the third day running at Carrington on Saturday morning, before United travelled on the team bus to their hotel where they had dinner and a pre-match meeting last night.

On Sunday he faces a massive first game as United boss in front of the cameras at Anfield at the end of a dizzying fortnight.

Recent findings suggest that with a stylish assist and a gorgeous goal, Viktor Gyokeres produced the sort of match-winning performance that suggests the Swedish striker is making significant progress at last. It has not always been straightforward for him at Arsenal, but this was unquestionably one of his better showings, and it continued an encouraging upturn in his form.

Gyokeres has been the second-choice striker for most of this season, with Mikel Arteta usually preferring the more subtle Kai Havertz in attack. There are signs, though, that Gyokeres is now growing in belief. Following this victory over Slavia Prague, which was much more narrow and nervy than it should have been, he has now scored two goals and registered three assists in his last five appearances.

Industry observers note that even more promising than those statistics was his all-round play in Prague. In the first half especially, Gyokeres held on to long passes, combined with his team-mates and tested the opposition with his runs in behind. For Arsenal’s first goal, he found Noni Madueke with a brilliant pass. For their second, he curled a fabulous strike into the top corner.

“Really good,” said Arteta of Gyokeres. “Not only the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s great news, because I think he needed that performance.”.

Sources indicate that those two moments in the first half eventually ensured another European victory for Arteta’s side, but the manager was far from impressed with the second-half showing. So smooth at first, Arsenal became remarkably ragged by the end. Slavia were deserving of their goal, scored by Wiktor Nowak. It looked like complacency had infected the minds of the Arsenal players, and you could feel Arteta’s fury radiating from the touchline.

It has been revealed that “We scored two goals and it should have been three, four or five,” said Arteta. “And at half-time the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game. Right from the beginning of the second half, we were extremely far from our standards in everything that we have to do, in every basic, in every concept, and in everything we discussed. So much to improve and I take full responsibility for that.”.

It has been revealed that without Gabriel Magalhães and David Raya, who both made dramatic stops on the goal-line, this could have become an ugly night for Arsenal against one of the weaker teams in the Champions League. The Czech side have now gone 23 games without a victory in Europe’s premier competition, which equals the longest winless run in European Cup history.

It has been revealed that it was a remarkable coincidence that this game fell on November 4, the exact date as the same fixture last season. On that occasion Arsenal were comfortable 3-0 winners, with Mikel Merino scoring twice, and they seemed to be heading towards a similar night when Madueke scored the early opener.

Sources indicate that the goal was made by Gyokeres, who held off a defender and then hooked an excellent pass into Madueke’s path. The Arsenal winger had already established his dominance over Oskar Kubiak, his opposite number, and he reached fifth gear before the Polish defender had even reached second. Madueke then slid his finish beneath the body of Nazar Domchak, Slavia’s teenage goalkeeper.

A fantastic pass from Gyökeres and a lovely finish from Madueke 🪄 The Arsenal attackers combine to great effect 🤝 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/blmMILZxok.

Just as Gyokeres is finding his form, so is Madueke. The absence of the injured Bukayo Saka has given Madueke a run in the side and he seems to be benefiting from it, even if he still lacks the same consistency in decision-making as his England team-mate.

One of Slavia’s many problems in a one-sided first half was their inability to cope with Arsenal’s rotations in midfield. Declan Rice, Martín Zubimendi and Merino were all alternating positions at will, taking turns to drop deep and push forward. Merino could have scored a couple, before he combined sharply with Gyokeres for Arsenal’s second.

Gyokeres has never been the most delicate link-up player, and there have been too many times when the ball has simply bounced off him, but here he was impressively sleek. A quick exchange of passes with Merino allowed him a sight of goal, and the curled finish was sumptuous. For a man known for his power, this was an uncharacteristic demonstration of finesse.

According to recent reports, game over? Arsenal clearly thought so. They certainly came out for the second half like a team that believed the job was done. Arteta became increasingly irate in the first few minutes after the restart, with Ben White on the receiving end of one verbal slap. Rice also received a telling-off, and a yellow card, from the referee after kicking the ball away in annoyance.

Would Slavia have secured a draw if they had been at full strength? They had been weakened by the banishment of their star striker from the club because of a series of disciplinary failings. Tomás Chory, the top scorer for the past two seasons, was chucked out of the team after showing his middle finger to the referee in a recent game. This sort of sanction would have earned Arteta’s approval, no doubt, but it did not increase Slavia’s chances of hurting the Premier League champions in those edgy final few minutes.

Sources indicate that perhaps they will reflect on that decision differently now, given the uncharacteristically wobbly second-half performance by Arsenal. The visitors were vulnerable in the latter stages, when they lacked the control and composure that Arteta expects. Gabriel, too, appeared dismayed by what he was seeing. At one point, he put his hands on his hips and scowled at his team-mates like an angry teacher.

With only a few minutes remaining, Nowak converted a left-wing cross to plunge Arsenal into a proper panic. It required a backs-to-the-wall defensive action, similar to the victory against Liverpool on Sunday, to get over the line.

Always we need to value winning away in the Champions League. It is extremely difficult. Two very different halves. We should have had three or four goals in the first half but we didn’t do it. Right at the start of the second half we were on the back foot, very sloppy and gave balls away. Then we had to suffer. A lot to learn.

We should have scored more in the first half and if we didn’t do that we had to go and do that in the second half.

Recent findings suggest that we made six changes but we know the quality of the players we have. Whether we were lacking something I don’t know but I would have done the same thing [again].

I value what the team has done now, it is 11 away games we played, but our standards should be higher.

Arteta on Gyokeres: "He was really good. A game we believed was good for him, for the spaces he could use. He was really connected to the team. Great news because I think he needed that. Really pleased.".

Arteta: "Two very different halves. The first we played at a really high level. At half-time the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game. Right from the beginning we were extremely far from our standards. Very far from the standards we expect from each other.".

First half we played really, really well. We created a lot of chances and could have scored more but the second half was completely different. They stepped up a gear and made it difficult for us and we have to learn from it. Delighted with the win but a lot of things to improve going forward.

In a recent development, maybe they started pressing a bit higher with more intensity. We had too many giveaways especially in the final third. There was too much running from box to box and we have to manage those reactions and go for the third and fourth goal.

At the end of the day it is three points.

Slavia Prague managed just one shot on goal in the first half worth 0.12 xG but finished the game with 18 shots on Arsenal’s goal and 2.23 xG. Arsenal could easily have dropped points on the balance of the second 45 minutes.

Quite surprised Declan Rice stayed on the pitch for the full 90 minutes there. He seemed to be in a bit of discomfort after a couple of long sprints. And then he got the silly yellow. Arteta perhaps panicking about the result.

37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1370 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border.
  • Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.
  • To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border. Yet, 37 years later, many people on both sides remain deeply skeptical of each other.

Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

We asked three artists from Germany with different perspectives on the history of the country's division to share their views.

Author Lea Streisand was born in 1979 and experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall firsthand while growing up in East Berlin.

In her books and essays, she has returned to her East German upbringing many times, using literature to process it.

The novel "Hufeland, at the corner of Bötzow" (2019, Ullstein), for example, recounts the period of reunification from a child's perspective.

Industry observers note that "November 9, 1989, was simply incredible," she told DW. She was 10 years old at the time. When her mother bought her winter boots with the 100 Deutsche Marks she received from the West German state — a welcome gift given to all East German citizens — she was so disappointed that she felt like crying. But later, a friend of her parents' let her buy so many sweets at the supermarket that they lasted until Christmas.

Sources indicate that "The disappointment really set in afterwards, with what happened over the course of the following year. It was unbelievable how rapidly an entire system was suddenly swept away and a new one built up, as if to say, 'There you go. You're welcome'," Streisand recalled. "I think it was just too fast for people.".

It has been revealed that the people of East Germany, or the GDR, had brought about the fall of the Berlin Wall themselves through a civil rights movement and numerous demonstrations. For many, however, the goal was not to dissolve the state immediately but to reform it.

Among them was Anke Feuchtenberger, born in 1963 in East Berlin. Her childhood was spent in East Berlin and in the East German region of Western Pomerania, where she now lives again and feels "very much at home.".

In a recent development, today, she teaches at the University of Applied Sciences in Hamburg, meaning she spends time on both sides of the former divide. Feuchtenberger is often described as Germany's most influential comic artist. Her work has also garnered international acclaim.

"Back then, as artists, we tried to bring about a change through posters and flyers — to gain more freedom without immediately abolishing socialism," she explained.

At the time, the fall of the Berlin Wall stirred up mixed feelings in Feuchtenberger: "I soon realized that the creative and revolutionary aspects of our movement were very quickly being smothered by consumerism, and that nationalist tendencies — which had already been noticeable before — were coming to the fore," Feuchtenberger recalled. "That made me afraid.".

Sources indicate that meanwhile, for photographic artist Simon Menner, born in 1978 in Emmendingen, in the West German state of Baden-Württemberg, Berlin was very far away. As Menner put it, he experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall as a child in a "rather abstract" way. Today, Berlin is his home.

Industry observers note that in his experience, the way films and documentaries portrayed East Germany around the time of reunification was very bleak. "But West Germany in the '80s," he remarked, "was also bleak and very staid.".

This uneven portrayal of the two parts of Germany is an problem that deeply concerns Menner — partly because he unwittingly contributed to it in a small way. Among other things, Menner's work explores the topic of surveillance and how it works.

In the archives of East Germany's Ministry for State Security, or Stasi — which are freely accessible today as part of the National Archives — he discovered a massive collection of photographs that both fascinated and horrified him and which he wanted to bring to the attention of a wider public.

Industry observers note that his photo book "Top Secret" (2012, from publisher Hatje Cantz) features a selection of photos that offer a unique insight into the work of the Stasi. Some are eerie, while others are curious or even absurd.

In a recent development, menner also tried to look into the photo archive of West Germany's Federal Intelligence Service. "I spent a year trying to gain access — without success," he mentioned.

In hindsight, he now finds his artistic project problematic because he believes it is too one-sided, focusing exclusively on East Germany's past.

According to Menner, West Germany's intelligence services in the 1960s were not exactly models of virtue either, and he believes it is "actually high time" to critically examine this part of history as well. In his view, an honest examination of Germany's past as a whole is a prerequisite for genuine reconciliation.

Sources indicate that streisand believes literature can help foster mutual understanding. "Literature opens a window into experiences we haven't had ourselves," she said. "You can immerse yourself in the mind of someone who has had a different life than you have and understand what happened.".

Industry observers note that interest in these stories remains strong. In 2023, Feuchtenberger published the nearly 500-page graphic novel "Comrade Cuckoo" (published by Reprodukt), which was the first graphic novel to be nominated for the Leipzig Book Fair Prize in the fiction category.

Sources indicate that the story spans a childhood in the fictional East German village of Pritschitanow in the 1960s in the GDR to the post-Reunification era. In it, Feuchtenberger weaves autobiographical memories of her upbringing with fantastical and fictional elements.

The artist said she was surprised "that, so long after the fall of the wall, my stories have sparked such great interest in the West.".

In particular, the fact that the main character, Kerstin, rarely sees her parents because they both work full-time is a topic that often comes up at readings. In the GDR, everyone had the right to work, she remarked. At the same time, it was a civic duty.

Could the West German interest in this stem from the fact that full-time employment for both parents has long been less common in the West? It's possible, said Feuchtenberger.

When looking toward their shared future, the two East German women are more optimistic than Menner, from West Germany.

According to recent reports, "In Berlin, I often don't even notice anymore whether I'm in the West or the East," mentioned Menner. "But when it comes to sociopolitical complications, politicians should listen to older and younger people more closely," he added, referring to the recent election successes of far-right Alternative for Germany, or AfD . "Otherwise, things are going to get difficult in the near future.".

"It's very important to step outside our own bubble because people all over the world are facing problems. Constantly focusing on this German-German divide that has emerged between the groups doesn't help," noted Feuchtenberger.

Industry observers note that "For me personally, the whole matter of borders has somehow dissolved," she explained. This is due in no small part to the many trips abroad that have taken her to various places around the world.

Industry observers note that moreover, in her hometown near the Polish border, she observes how animals couldn't care less about the border. "They come from the east and the west and do whatever they want," she noted. That's why she also gave "Comrade Cuckoo" the working title "A German Animal in a German Forest," "because I found the absurdity of an animal having a nationality so funny.".

In a recent development, "This East-West thing — our children won't have any interest in it at all," remarked Streisand. "Young people don't care where their parents come from. Can I get a job that will support a family? Do I have to go to war? Right now, completely different things are relevant.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A viral cold or bacterial infection can leave you feeling miserable, but each infection produces its own mix of symptoms.
  • The findings, many of which are unpublished, were presented on 15 November at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington DC, and challenge the established view of what it means to feel unwell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that researchers are beginning to show how neurons in the brain detect an infection and tailor physiological responses to fight it.Credit: Dr. Chris Henstridge/SPL.

A viral cold or bacterial infection can leave you feeling miserable, but each infection produces its own mix of symptoms. Now, neuroscientists are discovering that the brain is the conductor of these responses — decoding the type of pathogen that has invaded, accessing memories of past bouts of illness and even mobilizing immune defences at the sight of a sick person.

The findings, many of which are unpublished, were presented on 15 November at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington DC, and challenge the established view of what it means to feel unwell. Neuroscientists have long viewed neurological responses to infection as a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation, rather than a strategy tailored to the threat.

“Sickness is actually not a fixed program, although we often talk about it this way,” said Jessica Osterhout, a neurobiologist at the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, who chaired the session.

It has been revealed that A bacterial infection and a cold caused by a virus can both result in fever and exhaustion, yet they rarely trigger the same constellation of symptoms. Bacterial infections, for instance, tend to suppress appetite much more sharply than do colds, which made Osterhout and her colleagues wonder how the brain tells various pathogens apart.

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover.

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover.

Industry observers note that in unpublished experiments, Osterhout’s team compared mice injected with a bacterial toxin with those given a compound that mimics a viral infection. To see how the brain distinguished between pathogens, the researchers profiled individual cells in circumventricular organs, which are specialized structures with unusually permeable blood vessels that surround brain ventricles.

When the body has an infection, cells in the circumventricular organs switch on sets of immune-related genes and release distinct mixes of chemical signals. Those signals diffuse to nearby neurons and create distinct patterns of activity for different pathogens, allowing the brain to customize its symptom profile depending on the threat.

Rather than acting as conduits that let inflammatory signals pass unchecked from the blood into the wider brain, these structures “may actually interpret them”, Osterhout mentioned.

It has been revealed that sometimes, the brain doesn’t even wait for pathogens to enter the body to rally the immune system1. Andrea Serino, a neuroscientist at Lausanne University Hospital in Switzerland, studies how the brain maps peripersonal space, which is the area around the body roughly in arm’s reach.

Industry observers note that when Serino’s team placed volunteers in virtual reality, they found that threat-monitoring brain regions became active when avatars bearing skin lesions caused by viral or bacterial infections approached, even when the figures were beyond arm’s reach. Just 15 minutes of virtual exposure triggered a surge in frontline immune ‘sentinel’ cells in participants’ blood comparable to that induced by an influenza vaccine. This reaction did not occur when participants saw healthy-looking avatars or ones expressing fear.

These experiments suggest that the immune system uses “the predictive ability of the brain to react before pathogens enter the body”, Serino noted.

In a recent development, calcioMercato reports that Juventus have started monitoring Rayan Aït-Nouri ahead of the transfer market reopening, and the Manchester City left-back seems ready to listen. The Algeria international wants to restart his career elsewhere, views Turin favourably and has told his entourage to strengthen contacts, while the interest from Juventus is real and the club intends to act soon to test the deal’s feasibility.

Sources indicate that city want to sell outright and reinvest immediately, whereas Juventus prefer a loan with an option to buy, which suits a club bound by a UEFA settlement agreement. They first asked in August and City refused, while Gazzetta dello Sport indicates Luciano Spalletti wants competition for Andrea Cambiaso.

Recent findings suggest that city paid Wolves a reported £31m in June 2025 and gave him a contract until 2030, yet Enzo Maresca reportedly ranks the 25-year-old behind Joško Gvardiol and Nico O’Reilly. He had played 168 minutes in all competitions by mid-November, none of them in the Premier League, and his only starts have come in the EFL Cup.

According to recent reports, his strengths explain the fee. Aït-Nouri scored nine goals and set up 15 in 135 Premier League games for Wolves, added five assists in 1,605 minutes last season, and can also operate in central areas.

Recent findings suggest that the weakness is defensive security, because he is an ultra-attacking left-back. That matters now, with City on one point from their last four league games after losing 3-1 at Nottingham Forest and drawing 1-1 with Fulham on Saturday.

In a recent development, no, not in January, and not on terms that leave City carrying all the risk. Kevin De Bruyne has made his feelings for Manchester City crystal clear as he has spoken out for the first time since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations.

At the end of September, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

The Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts with a number of commercial partners to disguise secret funding of more than £830m and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

Man City continue to plead their innocence and lodged an appeal last month, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.”.

A plethora of possible sanctions have been mooted should Man City’s guilty verdict be upheld, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

De Bruyne spent 10 glorious years at the Etihad Stadium before leaving in the summer of 2025 and will go down as one of Man City’s greatest-ever players after playing a crucial role in the club winning 19 trophies during his time at the club.

The Belgian playmaker won six Premier League titles, five EFL Cups and three FA Cups, while he also won the Champions League during a historic treble-winning season in 2022-23.

The two-time Premier League Player of the Season scored 108 goals and provided 177 assists in 422 appearances for Man City across all competitions, with 119 of those assists recorded in the Premier League to rank him second on the all-time list behind Ryan Giggs (162).

De Bruyne has made a welcome retuned to Manchester as his current club Napoli prepare to face City in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

While De Bruyne has acknowledged that some people may have different opinions over Man City’s guilty verdict, the legendary midfielder himself has insisted that his feelings towards the club will “never change”.

"My feeling's never been different,” he told reporters at a press conference. “Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group. Of course, it's a lot of things that's been going on but I cannot change anything about that.

"I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly... This is my club! I love the owners, I've talked about a lot of stuff outside of football, I've even spoken to Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] how to buy a club and everything, so there's a lot of things that goes around after this.

In a recent development, "I've nothing but affection for this club and that will never change! Even now, the people who treated me for 10 years exceptionally, my family and everything, that's for me the most key and for me, that is it to be honest.".

Intense criticism has been aimed at Man City since the guilty verdict, but De Bruyne cannot "change anything" about people calling his former club a "disgrace" and still believes that everything he personally achieved with the club was won fairly.

It has been revealed that “It [the verdict] still doesn’t change, my football has not changed,” De Bruyne mentioned. “In life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit.

In a recent development, “I played in between the white lines, I competed with other players and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That’s the thing I value most.

“In my career, the most vital thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things.

“I’ve given my all and that’s not going to change in my mind. I don’t think a lot of ­people will change in their mind how they view me as a player or how we played. Other people may be disgraced a bit, but I can’t change anything about that.”.

Tuesday’s contest will mark De Bruyne’s second appearance back at the Etihad since departing Man City, and the 35-year-old will be hoping for a much smoother evening this time around.

On his previous visit last year, a first-half red card forced ex-Napoli boss Antonio Conte to reshuffle his side, with De Bruyne the unfortunate player to be sacrificed early in a 2-0 defeat.
