Industry observers note that como beat Cagliari 2-0 with two headers from Yan Couto crosses, moving back into fourth place on 26 points. Juventus visit next and trail the side holding the last Champions League place by eight points.

Como beat Cagliari 2-0 at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Saturday, 21 November 2026. Both goals were headers, and Yan Couto crossed for both of them. The result lifted Fàbregas’ side back into fourth place. That is the last Champions League place, and Juventus are the next visitors.

Ramón opened the scoring after 24 minutes. He met Couto’s cross from the right and headed past goalkeeper Caprile. Da Cunha, the captain, doubled the lead in the 56th minute. He headed in another Couto delivery from the centre of the area.

According to recent reports, fàbregas left Nico Paz and Perrone on the bench. The two Argentinians had rejoined the squad only hours before kick-off after international duty. Como play AEK in the Champions League on Tuesday. Even without the pair from the start, the hosts kept Cagliari out. Both men entered in the 57th minute, with Liberali and Milla making way respectively. It was Como’s first win since a defeat to Inter before the international break.

It has been revealed that for Fàbregas, the performance was not perfect, but he was very pleased. Perrone had a minor problem, the coach explained, which ruled out a full 90 minutes for the midfielder.

Como have now won three Serie A home games in a row without conceding, which they last did in October and November 1984, according to Sportmediaset. Da Cunha has three goals in his last four games across Serie A and the Champions League. Fàbregas has never lost to Cagliari in five Serie A matches as a coach. He has won three of them and drawn two. Cagliari have lost each of their last four away league games. That is their first run of four straight away defeats in Serie A since November–December 2023.

Como have eight wins, two draws and two defeats from 12 games, according to Como 1907. They have scored 20 goals and conceded 10.

Recent findings suggest that in that table, Juventus’ record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats. They have scored 15 goals and conceded 12. The gap to Como stood at eight points before Juventus’ game against Venezia.

Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (617 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.
  • "There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak noted after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.
  • "The IIHF as a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, don't hold it at all, or impose sanctions on Canada.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.

"There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak noted after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.

"The IIHF as a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, don't hold it at all, or impose sanctions on Canada.".

The threat comes after the Canadian government confirmed Wednesday that it would not allow Russian players to take part in the IIHF World Junior Championship starting on December 26 in Alberta.

"Canada's position is unequivocal: as long as Russia continues ⁠its war of aggression ​against Ukraine, there can be no return to business as usual," Adam van Koeverden, Canada's secretary of sport, said in a statement on Wednesday. "Canada will continue to stand with Ukraine.".

Following the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling in late October, in which it said the security concerns the IIHF cited for barring Russian teams from taking part in international tournaments was not sufficient, the world governing body pledged to work to comply with the decision.

On November 8, Norway stated it had been bumped from the World Juniors tournament and had been informed by the IIHF that Russia would take its place. Several other national hockey associations said they had received a revised schedule for the tournament and stated they would not play against Russia. The IIHF has not confirmed the change.

Germany has been watching developments related to the World Juniors and host nation Canada closely, as it is set to host the IIHF World Championship in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf starting on May 14.

With several nations saying they will not play Russia and major sponsors threatening to pull out, a German government spokesman described the prospect of hosting the tournament under these conditions as "effectively impossible.".

However, Germany has ruled out taking the Canadian approach.

Ronald Rauhe, Germany's minister of state for sport, stated Wednesday that refusing to grant visas was "not a solution for the [German] ice hockey federation [DEB], nor is it a solution for successfully hosting a world championship anywhere.".

At the same time, though, he expressed support for the DEB in its wish to host the tournament as planned.

"We believe that we should channel all our energy and efforts into helping sport — and ice hockey in particular — find a solution, which would, of course, entail excluding Russia from the World Championship.".

What makes things even more complicated for German officials are concerns that taking a hard-line on Russia could jeopardize Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

The thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees bidding to host an Olympic Games to follow its lead. The IOC is set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process.

For now, though, the ball appears to be in the IIHF's court, after Ottawa confirmed its refusal to grant Russians visas to play in the World Juniors. How the dispute regarding that tournament gets resolved could go a long way to finding a solution for the men's tournament in Germany in May.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Improvements in education, lifestyle and health during early life are slowing rates of cognitive decline in older people.Credit: Laura Olivas/Getty.

It has been revealed that people entering their golden years now have better memory and experience slower cognitive decline than previous generations. A study of people born between 1910 and 1964 found that a ten-year jump in birth date was associated with a 10% higher memory score at the age of 60. Researchers speculate that improvements in memory might be thanks to better education, health care and nutrition in childhood, while the slower decline in cognitive function might be influenced by factors later in life, such as improved treatment for cardiovascular and metabolic disease.

Reference: Nature Medicine paper.

Sources indicate that the large language models that underlie chatbots such as ChatGPT are rapidly overcoming some of their weaknesses, say computer scientists Owen Queen and James Zou. They analysed flaws — such as hallucinating references — that had been flagged by researchers in academic papers. Most flaws were no longer a problem within roughly 16 months of a paper’s publication — for example, the latest models hardly ever attribute information to sources that don’t exist. On the other hand, newer models are getting more sycophantic and worse at generating random numbers.

Reference: Owen Queen & James Zou blog post.

Sources indicate that undergraduate students were consistently the first group to start spreading emerging variants of the SARS-CoV-2 virus between 2021 and 2023, according to a massive genetic analysis. Researchers found that viral transmission during that period was highest among school students between the ages of 15 and 18, university undergrads and nursing-home residents. However, staff at all three types of institution had about the same risk of contracting COVID-19 as did those in their surrounding communities. The study’s scale “is truly impressive”, says infectious-disease researcher Bill Hanage.

A report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine (NASEM) suggests that science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, and standards for doing so are applied inconsistently across journals. NASEM recommends that the editorial review process be completed within 12 weeks for most cases and should rarely stretch beyond 6 months. The report was due to be published on 19 November, but was delayed after journalists at Science noted that it contained references with fabricated author names, which could suggest that artificial intelligence was used to draft or edit it.

Earlier this week we tried our hands at a game that tests our ability to decode ‘tortured phrases’ — ridiculous synonyms for common terms, which are intended to obscure plagiarism. For example, instead of ‘big data’, a study might use ‘colossal information’. The quiz inspired Briefing reader Chris Schneider to suggest her own tongue-in-cheek tortured phrase for our own dear ‘Nature Briefing’: “Essence of donning underwear.”.

In the spirit of silliness, we’d like to hear your best science-related tortured phrases — whether spotted in the wild or invented just for fun. Entertain us at briefing@nature.com.

Diptera — especially hoverflies (Syrphidae) — are undervalued pollinators. For example, on strawberry farms in England, hoverflies can make up more than half of the pollinating insects. Meanwhile, our reliance on managed honeybees can actually damage biodiversity and crop quality.

#174615. What's going on with the polar vortex?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

What's going on with the polar vortex?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (671 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, high up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons.
  • If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.
  • Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, high up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons. This is the polar vortex.

If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.

Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.

It's not yet clear how the current disruption to the polar vortex will affect the Northern Hemisphere winter, but scientists agree it is a record-breaking event.

"As far as we know, this is the earliest stratospheric vortex disruption that has been observed," European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecast (ECMWF) principal scientists Tim Stockdale and Frederic Vitart told the AFP news agency.

The French meteorological agency Meteo-France, meanwhile, called it "an unprecedented event.".

The early breakdown of the vortex "really increases the chance of cold air outbreaks across the latitudes where most of the densely populated population centers are across the Northern Hemisphere, US, Europe and East Asia," Judah Cohen, a climatologist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology told AFP.

The polar vortex is an enormous band of cold, low-pressure air that spins counterclockwise around the North Pole, about 10 to 50 kilometers (around 6 to 30 miles) above the surface.

It's closely connected to the jet stream, another band of powerful winds just below the vortex. The jet stream forms a boundary where the cold Arctic air meets warmer air from the tropics and subtropics.

The vortex can sometimes be a tight circle, keeping the coldest air locked around the North Pole over winter. It can also form uneven waves that dip southwards. And as it changes in strength and shape, that can influence the atmosphere below and alter the position of the jet stream, which drives the weather on the ground.

So, if the jet stream is more "wavy," and plunges south, it may also allow freezing Arctic air to spill southward.

One of the biggest influences that can provoke this kind of disruption is known as "sudden stratospheric warming." This is when temperatures in the polar stratosphere rise dramatically within a few days, causing the vortex's strong westerly winds to weaken.

This can push the vortex off its spot at the North Pole, make it split apart into multiple rings, or — as is happening now — cause the westerly winds to change direction.

It can take several weeks for the vortex to recover.

A previous polar vortex disruption contributed to the deadly Great Texas Freeze in February 2021, which caused more than a week of freezing temperatures that sparked power outages and killed hundreds of people.

But bone-chilling cold isn't a foregone conclusion. The Met Office, which is the UK's national weather and climate service, stresses that what's happening with the polar vortex can nudge odds in that direction, but it's not a switch that turns cold weather on and off.

Other weather patterns can also influence the outcome.

According to recent reports, for example, there's a possibility El Nino, which is associated with milder winters, could "moderate or modify" the impacts, Cohen told AFP. But he added this was not certain.

Recent findings suggest that the El Nino weather phenomenon, caused by the warming of surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is currently intensifying and is expected to peak at the end of the year. The ongoing event has been classified as exceptionally strong and is disrupting weather around the globe.

Industry observers note that some research has also linked the rapid warming of the Arctic driven by climate change to increasing disruptions to the polar vortex. That means that, even as the planet warms, some areas may still experience more severe cold spells. But this connection is not conclusive and is still debated by scientists.

Chelsea are lurching towards a crisis after yet another loss in which they were bullied, this time by Leeds United.

That 4-1 hiding saw Xabi Alonso heckled, and his players booed at both half-time and full-time, arguably deservedly so for such a disastrous showing.

It has led to tentative speculation around Alonso's future as Chelsea prepare to travel to Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest on Friday night, not to mention questions about where he is going wrong and how he might arrest his team's slump in form.

Here, Daily Mail Sport tackles all the burning issues at Stamford Bridge...

Chief among Chelsea’s problems is the fact they have conceded 20 Premier League goals this season. It is as many as they have scored at the other end. So, as much as we have enjoyed their freescoring forward line this season, so too must we criticise their disastrous defending.

We know Alonso can organise a defence. His Bayer Leverkusen side only conceded 24 goals when they won the Bundesliga as unbeaten champions in 2023-24. Chelsea are now on the verge of overtaking that total before we even hit December.

Liam Delap, their former striker now at Forest, will be desperate to add to that tally this Friday, too.

Xabi Alonso is coming under growing pressure, with his Chelsea side failing to back up their promising early-season form.

Levi Colwill was all at sea against Leeds as Chelsea shipped another four goals, taking their tally to 20 in 11 games.

Recent findings suggest that this morning, I watched back all 20 of the goals that Chelsea have leaked this term. There have been so many individual mistakes.

Like on day one, in the 3-2 win at Fulham, when an out of position Robert Sanchez let in Josh King's shot. And when Levi Colwill missed a defensive header which should have been routine, which led to Gonzalo Garcia scoring.

Chelsea got rid of Sanchez after that game, but Emiliano Martinez has hardly helped shore up this defence, as was apparent in the 4-1 loss to Leeds, when Colwill and Co were again all over the shop.

Until they cut out the silly mistakes, it is hard to see Chelsea competing at the top end of the Premier League.

Every manager at every club is sackable. Nobody is immune. But that’s not to say Alonso is suddenly up for the chop at Chelsea. I haven’t heard anything which would suggest those inside the club think finding a fourth permanent manager in the year 2026 is the answer.

Let’s not forget the overwhelming optimism when news broke of Chelsea striking an agreement to hire Alonso. It was an hour or so after the club had lost the 2026 FA Cup final to Manchester City. Recently, I took a look at the comments section of the story I wrote that day. It was full of excitement from Chelsea fans, and anger from Liverpool supporters at missing out on him.

Recent findings suggest that anyway, I think it’s too soon for us to start talking about Alonso’s job. He is in a bad moment, obviously. A very bad moment. Losing at home to Tottenham Hotspur and Leeds is a complete no-no for any Blues boss.

The supporters are more likely to curse his name than chant it right now, and it is hard to identify the style Alonso wants, with few discernible patterns of play to Chelsea's football.

But let’s give the bloke a chance to get himself out of this jam as he heads into his 12th Premier League match.

Recent findings suggest that believe it or not, Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it. Enzo Maresca resigned, exiting on January 1, 2026. Liam Rosenior was sacked, yes, but the club were effectively forced into that change as the players clearly gave up on him. Let’s see if Alonso can find some solutions.

Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it and Alonso, remember, has only had 11 Premier League games in charge.

We’ve tried to coax a little anger out of Alonso at press conferences, practically encouraging him to have a pop at his players for how they are performing, but he tends to resist the urge.

He’s clearly a nice guy. However, a Chelsea source does tell me he’s different behind the scenes. We may not see it on the outside, but internally, he is perfectly capable of being fiery with the players.

Which I hope is the case. Because sometimes, it can feel as if these Chelsea players need a good kick up the backside, rather than being coddled.

It has been revealed that I wrote a piece after the 4-1 loss to Leeds about how superstars can be stroppy. It’s normal. They can be so good that when the game isn’t going their way, they show their sulky side.

Palmer did that both during and after Saturday’s defeat. It was pretty poor from him to not want to go around applauding the fans who had bothered to stick around at full-time, even if there had been boos. An apology has been attributed to Palmer on social media, but that’s just another case of fake quotes being circulated.

For me, Palmer has to look at himself as much as anybody. It’s been too long since we’ve seen him try to take a match by the scruff of the neck.

Cole Palmer put in another quiet display against Leeds - he needs to start taking matches by the scruff of the neck.

WHAT HAPPENED WITH EMEGHA AFTER THE GAME?

Striker Emmanuel Emegha started for the first time and scored for the first time in Chelsea’s 4-1 loss to Leeds. Then he exited Stamford Bridge.

According to recent reports, we have seen players leaving the stadium on foot before. Videos of Palmer being surrounded by supporters while being escorted to his ride home occasionally crop up on social media.

Emegha had possessions stolen from his car while he was in a restaurant after the match and the incident has been reported to police. He was not harmed.

From a footballing point of view, I'd like to see Emegha start away at Forest this Friday.

Recent findings suggest that not that I’m aware. He’s been linked with Paris Saint-Germain and I had an email from a PR person this morning trying to push a loan to AC Milan or Roma as a possibility.

Alonso has given the fans what they wanted in the last few league games. He started Estevao against Manchester United, brought him on at half-time at Sunderland and started him against Leeds.

Estevao, clearly an exciting talent, could do with taking these opportunities to show why he deserves more of them.

Estevao has been given a chance to shine by Alonso in recent weeks but has failed to grab his opportunities.

I could see Malo Gusto leaving if there’s interest and Chelsea don’t keep demanding £75million, because it is hard to see who would spend that on him.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign. Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in the loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

I wouldn’t be surprised if a few other fringe players are linked with leaving in pursuit of game time ahead of January, such as Valentin Barco and Jamie Gittens, who is training again after his ankle injury.

It has been revealed that as for incomings, I don’t need to tell you that Chelsea are interested in Alex Scott of Bournemouth. Arsenal are, too, but the word is the Blues are still the frontrunners as we approach January. Whether Scott is what this team needs is another conversation.

After more than a month’s absence, Mile Svilar returned to the pitch, defending Roma’s goal in the match against Parma at the Tardini.

The Giallorossi number 99 then gave an interview to Cronache di Spogliatoio, discussing, among other topics, his relationship with De Rossi and Gasperini.

Industry observers note that the night against Feyenoord in the Europa League in 2024: “That night was the real start of my professional career. From there, everything changed. In those three games—the two against Feyenoord and the one against Frosinone—I started to be a professional. I once told my wife that many goalkeepers start out as second or third-choice, then start playing well due to injuries and start like that. Up until that point, it had happened to me many times in my early years at Benfica, a little less so at Roma, but I never had the feeling inside that it was the right time. “.

It has been revealed that “had the feeling that it could never happen to me. But that week, I had it, I felt that my moment had come. A feeling you can’t explain. I felt that something would happen like it does to the others. I knew it was the moment. I never mentioned it, but I knew it. I had a different adrenaline rush, the feeling of being crucial.”.

“In every job, you need someone who believes in you. And De Rossi was the person who believed in me, who gave me the push. He put me on the field, he had the power to change something, and Daniele changed my life, the life of my family.”.

“The week before his arrival, I played with AC Milan, but it ended a bit badly. Then we had Verona at home, and during the week I already knew I wouldn’t play. I wasn’t surprised. But he was the first person who called me into his office and remarked, ‘Look, Mile, I chose not to let you play and let Rui play. But in training, I saw something really interesting, so train because your time will come soon.’ For the first time, someone wanted to explain to me before the match and tell me I wouldn’t play. I immediately felt that he would be different for me.”.

“De Rossi’s dismissal hurt. I felt bad. He was someone who changed everything for me, in football and therefore in life. I will be grateful to him for the rest of my life.”.

“Last year was spectacular. But there were some low points, and many around us no longer believed in it. But when you keep doing, keep doing, like we’re doing with the coach, it’s something I’ve never seen.”.

“Gasperini’s biggest contribution? The mentality. The physical and tactical work the boys put in because it’s a different way of playing. There’s a winning mentality, which is what we needed because this club truly has everything it takes to do well.”.

Sources indicate that “Our objectives? It’s hard to say right now. As everyone can see, we’re doing really well. The tactical and physical work is putting a lot of us ahead. Maybe we were a little behind or something like that before, but now we’re moving up.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European leaders have so far found compromises in response to many of US President Donald Trump's demands.

But they were surprised to hear Trump say that he raised Europe's security framework with Russian officials.

"It's going to be a massive agreement and it's going to involve more than Ukraine," Trump noted after meeting Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House last week.

In a recent development, he noted that deal might include all of Europe. But what he meant by "all of Europe" was not clear.

US envoy Jared Kushner also wrote that Europe and Russia had struggled to establish a sustainable security framework for more than 30 years and that he was looking at "broader" European security architecture before he was to fly to Abu Dhabi.

That sent off alarm bells in European capitals, with diplomats having pushed back on Washington's approach to secure a peace deal in Ukraine.

They feared that a peace settlement could restore Russia's sphere of influence and undermine NATO.

"We ​already have European security ​architecture in place. NATO and the European Union both have their ​respective roles. We ​must make sure Ukraine is integrated ‌into ⁠this architecture," mentioned Kaja Kallas, the European Union's foreign policy chief.

Russia made clear during talks in Abu Dhabi earlier this week that they were keen to discuss a broader European security framework before tackling the specifics of the war.

"Phrases about the European security architecture are certainly Russian talking points and not only talking points but, to a degree, part of a media propaganda effort that Russia makes to frame the war as it wishes to frame the war," said Michael Kimmage, a historian of the Cold War.

Russian leaders, including Vladimir Putin, have long alleged that the US and NATO repeatedly violated pledges they made in the early 1990s not to expand the alliance into the former Soviet bloc.

They have seen NATO's enlargement during this period as having put them in a humiliating position in which they could do very little.

At the same time, in the 1990s, the European project saw the birth of the European Union, the single market that ensured the free movement of goods and people across member states, the Schengen agreement for border-free travel, and the euro.

The core idea was to extend peace across the continent.

It has been revealed that "Europe can mean so many things, but the European project was not designed for war. It was designed for peace," stated Kimmage.

During this period, there were even suggestions of Russia becoming a NATO member.

But that relative period of stability changed after Russia invaded Georgia in 2008, annexed Crimea in 2014 and launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Sources indicate that "Russia wants to redraw all of this by force. And I think that that's fundamentally unacceptable to Europe with all the diversity and variations that you get within the European landscape on what's acceptable and not acceptable. I think the large-scale redrawing of borders by force is just not the European project," stated Kimmage.

"So to the extent that the redrawing of borders by force is the lifeblood of Russian foreign policy, and I think that's a pretty easy case to make, Russia and Europe are at an impasse," he remarked.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Trump administration very promptly turned to making sure that "existing European security institutions" would be intact, with Jared Kushner having noted late Thursday that the next round of negotiations would include "our European partners.".

Kushner, along with Steve Witkoff, flew to Moscow to talk to Putin after talks in Abu Dhabi. Then they flew to Dublin, Ireland, to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Kushner had earlier Thursday signaled some "really incredible" postwar prepares for Ukraine, saying that it could not be concluded without Europeans at the table.

"We should not allow a diktat from Russia that would result in some kind of neutralization or significant reduction in the military forces of Ukraine going forward, because that would make Ukraine very, very vulnerable to future aggression and pressure coming from Russia," remarked Hiski Haukkala, the director of the Finnish Institute of International Affairs.

That would mean that Ukraine would also be completely dependent on the security guarantees that the US or Europeans are able and willing to provide.

In a recent development, "We are supporting Ukraine because we are supporting international law and the basic norms of decency and international security when it comes to European security architecture. And this is the vantage point from which we are operating," he mentioned.

The European Union has repeatedly pointed to some of the basic treaties that Russia broke, including:.

Industry observers note that "Russia walked away from these principles and smashed them to pieces in the process. And they are not interested in reinstating the previous security architecture order. They want something different in its stead. And as long as this is not on the table, the Russian form of negotiation is to wage war. War is a form of bargaining," Haukkala mentioned.

"And they are signaling strategic intent to change the makeup of European security, to subdue Ukraine and to change the very essence of European security," he added.

It has been revealed that daniel Fried, a former assistant secretary of state for European Affairs in the George W. Bush administration, noted Russia is very good at sticking to its demands.

He stated Russians know how to negotiate and "right now, they are not negotiating," referring to talks in Abu Dhabi.

Some experts stated there was no possibility of having a new security architecture with the Russians at this point because there was no trust or common vision to align with Russia at the moment.

"There is no obvious compromise — dismantling NATO and the EU is not an option for Europe," stated Maria Snegovaya, an expert on Russia at the Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank.

"Repeatedly offering Putin peace deals he is unwilling to accept will not produce that outcome," Snegovaya stated.

Others like Balazs Jarabik, an expert on post-Soviet politics, said that Russia was part of the European security architecture whether Europeans liked it or not.

"And the question is whether it's included as our enemy. Obviously, Russia is not going to be a partner, right? We have to find a modus operandi to reduce the risk of a horizontal escalation and potentially a bigger European war, even a bigger one than what we have now.".

A host of European leaders on Friday rejected the Russian demands to discuss Europe's security framework as well, with a spokesperson for the German government saying that Berlin was looking to host a meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" to secure funding for Ukraine's defense and reach a unified position regarding future peace talks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Six home wins from ten matches describe past results, not a 60% forecast for the next fixture.
  • Start by identifying the market you want to assess.
  • According to recent reports, use the same competition and season for both teams, while for the statistical source make sure to use the appropriate venue filter of your choice.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Six home wins from ten matches describe past results, not a 60% forecast for the next fixture. Before setting that record beside 1xbet football betting odds, check the strength of the opponents behind it. Compare the hosts’ home performances with the visitors’ away performances, then establish what those records suggest about your chosen market.

Start by identifying the market you want to assess. A home-win bet and a bet on the home team to score two or more goals have different requirements. For a home-win bet, the hosts must win the match. For a home team over 1.5 goals bet, the hosts must score at least two goals, regardless of the final result.

According to recent reports, use the same competition and season for both teams, while for the statistical source make sure to use the appropriate venue filter of your choice. Record:.

According to recent reports, for a team-goals bet, count how often the required total was reached. A team scoring six once and then recording five blanks has the same average as another scoring once in all six games. Only the first reached the two-goal threshold. Repeat the count for the visitors conceding at least two.

Keep the overall season record alongside the split. Three home fixtures give you little evidence of a lasting venue-specific pattern.

Suppose the two teams have these hypothetical records:.

However, it does not mean that because you’ve averaged these numbers, the home side is going to score 1.75 goals.

Since his arrival in Rome, Leonardo Balerdi has featured in every Champions League match.

The former Marseille player has logged a total of 223 minutes in the competition: 16 against Fenerbahçe, 27 against Real Madrid, and 90 minutes each against Slovan Bratislava and Manchester United.

However, the Argentine central defender may be forced to miss the away match against PSG.

During the game against Parma at the Stadio Tardini, the 25-year-old had to leave the pitch due to an ankle issue—a persistent problem that has been troubling him for weeks.

Ahead of tomorrow’s match between PSG and Roma, scheduled for 9:00 PM, Gian Piero Gasperini will need his entire squad available to try and contain the French side, with hopes of securing a significant result.

As reported by Il Messaggero, there are a few situations to monitor following the Parma match—including that of Leonardo Balerdi, who is dealing with an ankle matter.

Yesterday, the Argentine defender took part in only a portion of the group training session, alternating between work on the pitch and medical treatment.

There is cautious optimism regarding his inclusion in the squad to face PSG, but a final decision will only be made after the concluding training session, scheduled for 2:30 PM today. Meanwhile, medical tests are also expected today for Rensch, who is suffering from a flexor problem.

Artem Dovbyk also watched Bologna’s last match from the bench.

The Ukrainian center-back is still waiting for his first start for the Felsinei; first Tedesco and then Palladino aren’t impressed by the former Girona player. Quite the opposite.

The 1997-born player moved to the Rossoblu on loan this summer with an option to buy for €17 million, an option that will never be exercised and forces Roma to take direct interest to avoid further devaluing a €41 million investment.

The Capitoline club, therefore, is looking for the best solution for Dovbyk, who is increasingly distant from Bologna.

One of the issues to be resolved is his €3 million net salary, of which €2.5 million is paid by the Rossoblu. Interested clubs would have to pay half of that.

Industry observers note that dovbyk appears destined to leave Bologna. As reported by Resto del Carlino, Venezia is looking for a striker and has made contact to explore possible options for signing the Ukrainian striker.

According to recent reports, the 1997-born player’s agent, however, is scouting clubs in Spain. Dovbyk, in fact, was pichichi (top scorer) in La Liga before moving to Italy and beginning his downward spiral.

In a recent development, valencia is considering a move, but there’s work to be done given the player’s substantial salary, to which Bologna is paying 2.5 for the entire season. The Spanish club, if they acquire Dovbyk, could release Duro. The first moves ahead of the winter transfer window are underway.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roma continues to monitor the attacking market ahead of the winter transfer window, evaluating various opportunities to strengthen Gian Piero Gasperini’s attack.

Following rumors of interest in Endrick, another name has emerged that could fuel competition with AC Milan: Fotis Ioannidis, a 2000-born Greek striker at the moment playing for Sporting CP.

AC Milan is closely monitoring Ioannidis in their search for a centre-forward to replace Camarda, including the Greek among the options being evaluated along with Endrick and Tresoldi.

One potential player who could influence AC Milan’s interest is Ruben Amorim, who has previously worked with the striker at Sporting CP and knows his characteristics.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, Roma considers the player an interesting prospect, although they haven’t identified him as a top priority.

The European calendar will soon offer the Giallorossi the opportunity to observe the striker firsthand. On December 8th, Ioannidis will face Roma in the Champions League for Sporting CP, a match that could be an key opportunity to assess his qualities.

So far, the Greek has made 15 appearances this season, scoring two goals and providing two assists.

Gasperini, however, is primarily looking for a winger with acceleration, the ability to beat his man, and the ability to attack space—characteristics different from those of a central striker like the Greek. Therefore, any further exploration of Ioannidis will also depend on the opportunities that arise during the January transfer window.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Four wins in as many Champions League matches.

Twenty goals scored and an average of five goals per game. PSG are a steamroller, and tomorrow at the Parc des Princes, Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma will have to put in a legendary performance to emerge unscathed from a match that inevitably sees them as underdogs.

On the eve of the match, Luis Enrique spoke at a press conference and outlined tomorrow’s battle against the Roman side.

On his memories from his brief spell in Rome, Enrique said, “It’s been 15 years since then, and it was a very special experience for me. I have fond memories of my year in Rome. I get a wonderful feeling every time I have the chance to visit Rome. It’s a magnificent city, and I’m happy. Of course, things can go better or worse, but that’s life, and you have to accept it. My memories of Rome are very positive.”.

Sources indicate that “I think Gasperini is a very experienced coach. I really like him because his teams have a very clear identity and style of play, very different from what we’re used to. I remember when I was in Rome he was at Inter. It was his first year at Inter, and it didn’t end well for him because Inter didn’t have the confidence to keep a coach like Gasperini.”.

Recent findings suggest that “He’s proven his worth and is a top-notch coach. I like watching this type of coach, and as a coach, it’s a motivation for me to observe Gasperini’s teams. Tomorrow we’ll face some difficulties; we’ll see what kind of team they are and their particular way of defending. It’s very different from what we’re used to. It’ll be a great challenge to face.”.

“I think Gasperini is clearly a phoenix of Italian football. He has a very different way of looking at football, which I like because he tries to constantly attack and be better than the opponent. His teams constantly press, and it’s unusual to see that in Italian football. He’s remained true to his way of understanding football. His team has a recognizable identity and very different characteristics from the others. They’re very physical, but at the same time they have quality players. If, as a coach, you have the ability to convince your quality players to do the defensive work, it means you’re a top-notch coach. It’s wonderful to have coaches like him, and, I repeat, I’m an admirer of Gasperini.”.

#174600. Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (934 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Young people across Germany and Europe are taking to the streets, voicing fears of a bleak future.
  • Recent findings suggest that but is that really the case?
  • "Of course, it's fair to ask, 'Were things just as tough for you back then?'" youth researcher Simon Schnetzer tells DW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Young people across Germany and Europe are taking to the streets, voicing fears of a bleak future.

Recent findings suggest that but is that really the case? Does Gen Z face greater challenges than Baby Boomers did in the 1990s? What do the two generations have in common, and where do their experiences differ?

"Of course, it's fair to ask, 'Were things just as tough for you back then?'" youth researcher Simon Schnetzer tells DW. "But young people see that things are difficult for them now, and say that's why they need support today.".

Schnetzer, who wrote the annual Youth in Germany study, highlights one key question raised by the recent demonstrations across Europe as: "Have we given young people the conditions they need to live and work here with confidence, and to keep this system funded?".

Sources indicate that his straightforward answer is no. A survey of the statistics shows that both Gen Z and the Baby Boomers are affected by major societal changes, but in different ways. DW surveyed data on pensions, education, housing and climate change to find out more.

Sources indicate that the facts point to a clear trend: Fewer and fewer young people are having to support an ever-growing number of retirees. According to the Germany's public pension insurance system, there were 3.73 contributors for every retiree in 1957. By 2025, that figure had fallen to just 2.1.

According to recent reports, by 2045, this number is projected to drop to just 1.73 contributors per retiree. In absolute terms, this means 35.35 million contributors will be financing pensions for 16.82 million retirees.

To cushion this trend and keep contribution rates stable, the pension system already receives around €118 billion [$131 billion] in annual government subsidies. This amounts to roughly 25% of the federal budget. That means an increasing share of the population will be called upon to help fund pensions.

There are also signs that many people's pensions are already falling short of covering their living expenses. The number of retirees relying on federal basic income support has risen from 257,000 in 2003 to 738,000 in 2024.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Rising rents hit low-income households particularly hard. According to a report by the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW), the share of income spent on rent by low-income households rose from around 24% in 1990 to nearly 36% in 2021.

This means that in 2021, the lowest-income households spent an average of 14 percentage points more of their income on rent than high-income households.

According to Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), in 2025, an average of 11% of the population spent more than 40% of their disposable income on housing costs. Among people at risk of poverty, the figure was as high as 35%.

It has been revealed that however, according to calculations by real estate platform Jacasa, Boomers could actually help ease pressure on the housing market in the coming years. They right now own around 4.8 million owner-occupied houses and apartments.

Over the coming decades, these properties are expected to change hands as former occupants sell them, move into assisted living, or hand them down through inheritance. In some regions, this could lead to an oversupply of properties and, consequently, lower prices, according to Jacasa's projections.

According to the federal government's Education Finance Report, public spending on education for people under 30 has doubled since 2011, rising from around €4,000 to approximately €8,000 per person annually.

Sources indicate that despite this increase, Germany ranks only in the middle of the pack internationally. According to the Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), public education spending accounted for 4.6% of Germany's gross domestic product (GDP) in 2022, compared with an OECD average of 4.7%.

Sources indicate that however, the additional funding cannot solve the problem of teacher shortages. According to estimates by the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs, Germany will be short of around 27,000 teachers by 2035. The main reasons are the wave of Baby Boomer retirements and declining birth rates, which have contributed to a shortage of young teachers.

Back in 1972, the Club of Rome warned of the consequences of global warming in its landmark publication The Limits to Growth. According to the United Nations, the planet is on track for 2.6°C of warming by the end of the century compared with pre-industrial levels.

If the world maintains its current climate policies, children who are six years old today could experience heat waves two to seven times as often as Boomers did over their lifetimes. That was the finding of a 2025 study by Vrije University in Brussels.

Recent findings suggest that the deadly impact of extreme weather is already evident in rising death tolls during recent heatwaves. According to Germany's Robert Koch Institute (RKI), an estimated 16,000 people died from heat-related causes across Germany by mid-September 2026. The vast majority — more than 14,000 — were over the age of 65.

In a recent development, "Gen Z and Baby Boomers are in the same boat. We need to bring them together, because otherwise younger people have no prospects for prosperity, and neither do older generations," youth researcher Schnetzer concludes.

Sources indicate that he suggests that both generations take to the streets and protest together, adding that would just be the beginning. "What needs to follow is a constructive process to define goals and measures that everyone can support," he said. "Even if it means making sacrifices.".

#174598. Breaking: Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics

Breaking: Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1094 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, when police officers appeared at her home in Istanbul last Wednesday evening, Yonca Verdioglu Sik was surprised — even more so when they took her in for questioning.
  • But, according to transcripts of the interrogation that were published later, Verdioglu Sik was never asked any questions about espionage.
  • Industry observers note that for 18 years, Verdioglu Sik, who was born and raised in Germany, has been the foundation's project coordinator.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, when police officers appeared at her home in Istanbul last Wednesday evening, Yonca Verdioglu Sik was surprised — even more so when they took her in for questioning. Her lawyer says she was accused of political and military espionage.

But, according to transcripts of the interrogation that were published later, Verdioglu Sik was never asked any questions about espionage. Instead the public prosecutor's office appeared to be more interested in the activities of her German employer, the Heinrich Böll Foundation.

Industry observers note that for 18 years, Verdioglu Sik, who was born and raised in Germany, has been the foundation's project coordinator. In her role, she organizes projects that focus on democracy and the rights of women, minorities and LGBTQ+ people.

During the interrogation, transfers of money from the foundation into her bank account were discussed. Verdioglu Sik found out that she was now also subject to a travel ban.

Verdioglu Sik was eventually released, but her arrest caused outrage among critics of the Turkish government. She is married to investigative journalist and member of parliament, Ahmet Sik. He belongs to the left-wing Workers' Party of Turkey, or TIP, and is known as one of the harshest critics of the current government.

Sik has recently been looking into a stock market scandal, which allegedly benefited members of the ruling Justice and Development Party, or AKP, headed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and associates.

Opposition critics drew a clear conclusion: As a member of parliament, Sik has parliamentary immunity. So instead, the justice system is putting pressure on him through his wife.

"If you take away a state's law, what is left is no longer called a state, but a gang," Sik responded to the arrest in writing.

Verdioglu Sik's arrest is not the first such case in Turkey. Ever since the attempted coup against the Erdogan government in 2016, accusations of espionage have been leveled at a wide variety of groups in Turkey: journalists, opposition figures and human rights activists as well as employees of foreign embassies and staff of foreign institutions like nongovernmental organizations and foundations.

Sources indicate that such accusations have often been followed by acquittals or convictions for other offenses, albeit sometimes years later. But what the many instances have in common is what's known as a "chilling effect." Any investigation can mean lengthy pre-trial detention, reputational and professional damage and even social isolation.

In the past, such cases have even triggered diplomatic spats.

Sources indicate that in 2015, for example, Can Dundar and Erdem Gul, both senior journalists at the opposition daily Cumhuriyet, were accused of espionage after reporting that Turkey had tried to ship arms to rebels fighting the Syrian government. Dundar now lives in exile in Berlin.

In 2017, Erdogan said that reporter Deniz Yücel, then working for German newspaper Die Welt, was a "German agent." That led to a serious diplomatic crisis between Berlin and Ankara.

Espionage charges have also been laid against local employees of the US diplomatic corps and against a lawyer working for the German embassy. US pastor Andrew Brunson and his wife were also arrested because of alleged links to Kurdish anti-government groups. Turkish philanthropist and human rights activist Osman Kavala, who was charged with espionage and attempting to overthrow the constitutional order, remains in prison.

Most recently, espionage charges have been brought against the former Istanbul mayor and Erdogan's political competitor, Ekrem Imamoglu, and a number of journalists.

Hakki Tas, a research fellow and expert on Turkey at the German Institute for Global and Area Studies, stated the number of such cases have been increasing over the past few years.

In a recent development, on the one hand, Turkey has the right to protect itself from foreign intelligence services — especially given geopolitical competition and conflict in the region, he argued. On the other hand, there's a long tradition of bringing the Turkish opposition to court to face security charges.

"What foreigners or employees of foreign institutions have experienced in recent years is a continuation of this pattern," Tas told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that media outlets and NGOs critical of the government have faced investigations, trials and other sorts of state sanctions for years. The ruling AKP party has also brought in its own version of a so-called "foreign agent law.".

These sorts of espionage cases serve both a domestic and foreign policy function, Tas said.

For locals, "contact with a foreign institution, foreign funding or even a perfectly normal salary could become part of an investigation someday," he explained. "For opposition figures and civil society organizations, in particular, this can become a security matter.".

Recent findings suggest that in terms of foreign policy, the cases also show other countries that there are limits to their activities inside Turkey. These kinds of accusations seem to become more frequent when there's some sort of foreign policy tension — for example, after Western criticism of how opposition groups were dealt with after the alleged coup in 2016, the aforementioned disputes about arms deliveries in connection with Syria, or criticism from abroad about the removal of elected mayors in Turkey.

It can also serve as a kind of "hostage diplomacy," Tas said.

According to recent reports, the case of US pastor Brunson is a good example. After his arrest, the Turkish government proposed a trade with the Americans. They wanted to exchange Turkish preacher Fethullah Gulen, who lived in the US and who the Turkish government blamed for the 2016 coup attempt.

It has been revealed that this suspicion of foreign institutions isn't something that the Erdogan government invented, Tas points out. In the early 2000s, several representatives of German organizations were already made to stand trial in Turkey. At the time, it was alleged that, among other things, the German spy service was using German foundations as a front for conspiracy.

In some of the best-known cases, defendants often don't end up convicted of espionage. In the case of activist Osman Kavala, he was initially acquitted of espionage several times and spent two years in prison, just because of those charges.

But Tas noted that's no surprise, referring to a 1979 work about the sociology of law written by US law professor Malcolm Feeley. It's title: "The Process Is the Punishment.".

He will hope to be back in the starting line-up by the time Hibernian face Rangers in the Scottish League Cup final next month.

Wheatley was linked with a permanent move to Everton in the summer, but United ultimately decided to send him on loan to Championship side Lincoln City.

The striker made his debut off the bench in a Carabao Cup tie against Blackpool, but then picked up an injury that put him on the sidelines.

He recently returned to full fitness and made his Championship debut, playing 59 minutes in a 1-0 defeat at home to Wrexham.

It has been revealed that “There were some flashes of what he’s capable of,” head coach Tom Shaw said. “Ethan, obviously that’s his first start, he’s not had loads of football, but he’s a high-potential young player. He’s got good athleticism, good quality.

According to recent reports, “Perhaps he didn’t have enough of those moments and situations to show that today, but we know that the threat is there. That’ll be really good for him, the 60 minutes and the experience.”.

Having starred for Arsenal’s academy, Chido Obi arrived at United in 2024 with a reputation as one of football’s most exciting young talents.

The striker made eight first-team appearances in his debut season, but remained with United’s youth sides throughout the 2025-26 campaign.

He joined newly-promoted Eredivisie side Willem II in the summer in search of regular first-team football, but the loan move has not gone to initiative.

The 18-year-old has no goals to his name and is yet to start a single game for the club, with all seven of his appearances to date coming off the substitutes’ bench.

He also faced criticism for his lack of defensive work after Willem II went down to 10 men in a domestic cup win over Helmond Sport.

Sources indicate that “It is partly a matter of mindset, but also of youthful exuberance,” then-caretaker manager Adrie Koster stated. “That boy has never experienced anything like this before.

“He doesn’t do it on purpose either, so we shouldn’t focus everything on him. This is simply part of his learning process. But we are going to talk to him about it.”.

United are set to consider recalling the Denmark Under-21 international in the January transfer window.

💡 Key Takeaways

It is a celebration of the freedom he once so painfully lacked in the former East Germany, and of the freedom people around the world still yearn for.
  • Sources indicate that these themes run throughout Wolf Biermann's new album "Unterm Haar nur Himmel" ("Beneath Hair, Only Sky") released to mark his 90th birthday.
  • Biermann remains one of Germany's most influential singer-songwriters, and at 90, he shows little sign of putting down his guitar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

He mocks Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as "political lovers," denounces the "endless fratricidal war" over the Palestinian territories, and repeatedly invokes "Lady Liberty." It is a celebration of the freedom he once so painfully lacked in the former East Germany, and of the freedom people around the world still yearn for.

Sources indicate that these themes run throughout Wolf Biermann's new album "Unterm Haar nur Himmel" ("Beneath Hair, Only Sky") released to mark his 90th birthday. The album's title is a characteristically poetic phrase coined by Biermann himself. It evokes the idea that however restrictive the world may become, the human mind and spirit remain free. Beneath the hair lies open sky: a metaphor for inner freedom, independence and imagination.

Biermann remains one of Germany's most influential singer-songwriters, and at 90, he shows little sign of putting down his guitar. Often described as Germany's answer to Bob Dylan, the outspoken troubadour continues to weigh in on the complications shaping the world today.

Sources indicate that in his recent song "Moritat von den Liebespaaren" ("Ballad of the Lovers"), he delivers a simple but urgent message: no single person can save the world, yet everyone can help make it a better place. Above all, the song is a call to take responsibility for one's own life rather than remain a bystander.

This outspokenness was instilled in Biermann early on. When he was born in Hamburg in 1936, Adolf Hitler was already in power. His father was a dockworker, a committed communist, a resistance fighter against the Nazis — and Jewish.

Wolf was just three months old when the Gestapo, Hitler's secret police, arrested his father. He initially served time in prison before he was murdered by the Nazis at Auschwitz in early 1943.

Just a few months later, British and American bombers attacked Hamburg, unleashing a devastating firestorm. "Nothing in my life has shaped me more," Biermann has repeatedly noted in interviews. When the sirens sounded, his mother took him into an air raid shelter. The house above them was burning.

Yet Biermann has said his memories of that time are rooted in a profound sense of trust in life. In an interview with the German magazine Chrismon, he recalled: "I pressed my face into my mother's soft coat so I could breathe. A sense of security in the midst of the end of the world. We stumbled out over the neighboring house and into the open. The firestorm lifted a burning roof into the air. Roaring corrugated metal, smoke everywhere. We searched for a way out. [...] Death was everywhere. 40,000 people died. They had no chance. But I did. My strong mama.".

Industry observers note that biermann's mother instilled communist and anti-fascist ideas in him with almost religious fervor. "My mother had only one goal after those dark years," Biermann once recalled. "I was supposed to survive so that I could, as she put it rather grandly, one day take revenge for my father's death. I was supposed to build communism.".

Industry observers note that in 1953, while countless people were fleeing East Germany, Biermann moved there of his own free will — after all, communism was the official state ideology. He was just 16 at the time. In East Berlin, he studied political economy, mathematics and philosophy. His role models were writers Bertolt Brecht and Heinrich Heine. He began working as an assistant director at the Berliner Ensemble, and also began writing and performing his political songs.

In a recent development, biermann soon realized that life in East Germany was far from the communist paradise he had imagined and he wrote about this openly in his songs. "The party bosses were torn," Biermann noted. "They were delighted by this young poet who could play the guitar so beautifully and sing such cheeky songs. They thought they just needed to bring me into line. Even today, I'm amazed that I wound up cast in the role of the heroic dragon slayer.".

Sources indicate that in 1965, East Germany's ruling Socialist Unity Party, the SED, imposed a blanket ban on Biermann performing or publishing his work. His East Berlin apartment, which was under constant surveillance, soon became a gathering place for dissidents and critical thinkers.

Industry observers note that yet, to his great surprise, the East German authorities allowed him to travel to Cologne, West Germany in 1976. There, around 7,000 people flocked to see him. For four and a half hours, he strummed and sang, mocking the East German regime. His songs were so popular that bootleg copies found their way back to East Germany.

It has been revealed that on November 16, while still on tour in West Germany, Biermann heard the news on his car radio that he had been stripped of his right to continue residing in the German Democratic Republic. The regime accused him of betraying and slandering East Germany. ".

I felt like the ground had opened up beneath me. I was overcome with fear, everything went dark," Biermann wrote in his memoirs.

In a petition, leading East German intellectuals spoke out against the decision. In response, the regime stepped up surveillance of dissidents, imposed professional bans and jailed its critics. Several prominent public figures left the country.

Sources indicate that "The SED leadership expected an angry media response from the West. What they hadn't reckoned with was that, for the very first time, a group of respected East German writers and artists would make their protest public, disguising it as a humble petition," Biermann wrote.

Afterward, Biermann sank into a deep depression. "Not just because I had been torn away from the friends I knew and loved in East Berlin, but also because I had lost my familiar mortal enemies," he said.

According to recent reports, he became involved in the peace and anti-nuclear movements and continued singing about the injustices of the world. "The world's conflicts take different forms in each generation," he said. "But it's always the same struggle for freedom.".

It has been revealed that the singer-songwriter looks to spend his 90th birthday at home in Hamburg with his wife and manager, Pamela. For the first time in his life, he stated, he's skipping the birthday party, even with his 10 children.

"I'm so old and I can feel my strength fading. And I know that the next day I have a major concert at the Berliner Ensemble," he told the German Press Agency.

And should he ever die, he noted, he wants to be buried at Berlin's cemetery where some renowned German writers and intellectuals have been laid to rest, among them Bertolt Brecht, Anna Seghers and Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel. He still has a thing or two to discuss with them.

This article was originally written in German.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine (NASEM) finds.
  • Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A statue of Albert Einstein holding a scientific manuscript sits outside the US National Academy of Sciences building in Washington DC.Credit: Paul J. Richards/AFP via Getty.

According to recent reports, science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine (NASEM) finds. Standards for fixing errors are also inconsistently applied across research journals, it says.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.

There are no data on how long retraction or correction at the moment takes, as journals do not generally disclose when they were alerted to a problem in a paper; the NASEM report indicates they should. On average, according to the Retraction Watch database, retractions occur around 2.4 years after a paper is published. The report recommends that editorial review processes be completed within 12 weeks for most cases and should rarely stretch beyond 6 months — at least when editors are looking at concerns over a single paper.

“The big picture is, the process is too slow,” notes Randy Schekman, a cell biologist at the University of California, Berkeley, who chaired the 14-person committee that produced the NASEM report. A prompter and more transparent process would strengthen the reliability of the scientific record, he says.

The report was due to be published online on 19 November, but publication was delayed after journalists at Science noted that it contained some references with fabricated first names for authors, a possible sign that large language models had been used to write or edit the material and had been insufficiently checked.

“It's unfortunate that there were these flawed references in a report about fixing the literature,” claims Jennifer Byrne, a cancer researcher and research integrity sleuth at the University of Sydney who first flagged the concern to Science when reviewing the report, which was shared ahead of publication with media outlets.

It has been revealed that the report had two main aims: to speed up the process of retraction or correction and to lower the “tremendous emotional barriers” for authors to correct honest mistakes in the record, Schekman indicates. “Part of the problem is that it’s too rare for a paper to be retracted,” he adds.

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

It has been revealed that the report also suggests that journals shouldn’t just wait for complaints to reach them, but instead “take proactive steps” to identify errors and integrity complications. That might include journal-wide audits, or regularly monitoring social media and online platforms where post-publication issues are raised, it notes.

Existing guidelines for publishers, such as those from the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) in London, only urge a “timely” response to concerns without setting out expected schedules, and don’t suggest journals scan online platforms for complaints.

“A major theme running through the report is that we have to distinguish between retraction or correction, and research misconduct,” notes Dorothy Bishop, a research-integrity sleuth in Oxford, UK, who was on the NASEM committee. Authors shouldn’t associate retracting a paper with the stigma of misconduct, she indicates. And although journal editors sometimes wait for a university to investigate whether there is research misconduct before correcting a paper, they shouldn’t, she adds.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a newly introduced record.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a fresh record.

Calls for changing these attitudes aren’t new: journals have long emphasized that retractions can cover honest mistakes. When it comes to journal processes, Holden Thorpe, the editor in chief of Science, urged that issuing corrections or retractions and making a determination of misconduct be separated in an editorial in 2022, and COPE guidelines already emphasize the point. But “there are still plenty of people who see a correction or retraction as an allegation of fraud,” indicates Thorpe, who was also on the NASEM committee. “Hopefully, this report will accelerate the recognition of the distinction,” he says.

Tarkowski was shown the red for the follow-through on a tackle on Brentford’s Yehor Yarmolyuk which saw his name crossed off a list of players who have surprisingly never received a red.

Here are the remaining candidates:.

A career of 323 games and not a single red card is an impressive feat from King.

The former Tottenham defender’s struggles with injuries are well known with him only twice playing more than 30 Premier League games in a single season but when he was on the pitch, he was as composed as can be.

Not only did King never get his marching orders, he only got nine yellows in every match he played.

King’s numbers are impressive, but the record belongs to Hughes.

The former Newcastle, Fulham and Aston Villa man played 455 Premier League matches but never received a red card.

In total, the Northern Irishman played 675 games in his career and was never sent off, earning 19 yellows in that time.

Considering how composed he often looked, perhaps we could not be too surprised that Lahm features on this list.

He played in eight different positions in his career but never once was so out of his depth that he got himself sent off.

Lahm primarily operated as a full-back with 269 appearances on the right and 219 on the left before Pep Guardiola converted him into a defensive midfielder.

He did quite like a yellow though, getting 49 in his career.

Considering he played the majority of his career as a sweeper, it is particularly impressive that Italian legend Scirea was never sent off.

The World Cup and European Cup-winning defender played 621 times and yet was never given his marching orders.

To make it even more impressive, in his long career, which featured 551 games for Juventus, Scirea got just four yellow cards.

The former Match of the Day host is well known for having not only never received a red, but never even got booked either.

Lineker played 468 games, the majority of which were in the First Division, and yes he was a striker but we could show you a long list of number nines who have picked up a red.

The closest Lineker ever came was in Euro 1992 when he stamped on Basile Boli’s toe. The ref missed it and the pre-VAR world meant Lineker was in the clear.

Not only did Barnes never receive a red, but he was also the first player to make it past 100 Premier League games without a card of either colour.

Barnes played most of his football pre-Premier League, getting 349 appearances in the old First Division before making 201 in the Premier League, but never got a red.

He ended his career with 696 games played and not a single entry in the referee’s book.

Iniesta getting a red card just feels wrong, doesn’t it? Well, the good news is it’s never happened.

Iniesta played 885 games in his career, 674 of which were for Barcelona, but never received a red card.

He did pick up a fair few yellows, having got 74 in his time.

Considering he was quite a robust winger, Duff being on this list is surprising.

He played 629 games, starting off with Blackburn before moving to Chelsea in 2003, yet never got a red card.

Instead, he got 42 yellows, the majority of which came with Rovers, but he was largely a clean player.

The club added in a statement: “Leeds United condemns this behaviour in the strongest possible terms. There is no place for racism in football or society.

“The club will work with the Premier League and relevant authorities to identify the individuals and push for the strongest possible action to be taken against them.

“Jayden has the full and unconditional support of the club and his team-mates, and we all stand with him at this time. Nobody should ever be subjected to racist abuse.”.

Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, described Bogle as the “softest player” in the Premier League who would never try to hurt an opponent.

Referee John Brooks did not issue a yellow card, with VAR Tony Harrington sticking with the on-field decision.

Sources indicate that “I’m confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There’s a lack of speed going into the challenge and he’s stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge,” Harrington was quoted on the substantial screen at Elland Road.

Tottenham will make a formal complaint to Pro Ref over the decision not to send off Bogle.

“I haven’t watched the scenes back so I can’t give you a clear opinion, out of the game it looked a handball but the scene with Jayden was not too far away from my bench and it looked a very unlucky coming together,” Farke said.

“Fingers crossed for Mathys that he is back soon, but it looked like there was not much speed in this action, but Jayden Bogle is one of the most fair players in the country, he would never injure or foul a player on purpose because he is such a fair character.”.

De Zerbi had warned his team they would face a hostile atmosphere at Elland Road, but instead of rising to the challenge, Spurs were passive until it was too late.

“We didn’t win any duels, we didn’t win any one-to-ones, there was space to play and we didn’t take the right position,” De Zerbi remarked. “We didn’t show personality, we didn’t show what we are or who we are. Leeds United are heartbroken to learn of the passing of supporter Colin Westby at the age of 68. Colin suffered a medical emergency ahead of our Premier League fixture with Manchester United on Sunday 18 October at Elland Road. After being transferred to hospital, he was placed into a medically induced coma and sadly following a period of unresponsiveness, the decision was made to withdraw life support. Colin was a long-standing Season Ticket Holder at the club, attending matches for over 50 years. The thoughts of everyone at Leeds United are with Colin's family and friends at this sad time. We will pay tribute to Colin in the 68th minute of our next Premier League fixture with Tottenham Hotspur, on Saturday 7 November.

Sources indicate that good morning and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Leeds United and Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road. The home side, lions at night and mice in the morning, have the unenviable record of 21 top-flight matches with a kick-off time before 3pm without a win. All that extra TV moolah comes in handy but their home ground, a bearpit under the floodlights, is neutered when its denizens are yawning instead of being fired up by social lubricant.

According to recent reports, daniel Farke’s team started the campaign well but are now without a win in five, drawing three matches with teams beneath them in the table – Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Sunderland – and  losing to two above them, Arsenal and Bournemouth. In fairness they played well against the champions for an hour and were deservedly in the lead until Mikel Arteta turnd to his billionaire’s bench and changed the game. At Bournemouth last week they also made a decent start, had a goal disallowed for striking Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s arm and then James Trafford chucked one in.

Industry observers note that they never recovered, found themselves increasingly bogged down when trying to unlock a low block and were mugged on the break in added time to lose 2-0. They are a robust side overly reliant on their wing-backs to create chances for their No 9 in the absence of the injured Noah Okafor who was unavailable to train with the team this week because of a groin injury but may be fit enough for the bench.

Spurs, by contrast, are buoyant following three wins on the bounce – over Coventry, Chelsea and Palace, two with clean sheets – that has taken them from 19th to ninth, three places above Leeds. They have won their last three visits to Elland Road, 0-4 under Antonio Conte, which proved to be the last match of Marcelo Bielsa’s glorious spell at the Peacocks, 1-4 under Ryan Mason, which sealed Leeds’ relegation, and 1-2 under Tomas Frank last year by virtue of goals from Mathys Tel and Mohammed Kudus as the home side struggled against their width back in the days before their switch to a back three.

Sources indicate that tel also scored in Spurs’ home game, a 1-1 draw in May, and then kicked Ethan Ampadu in the head to concede the penalty from which Leeds equalised.
